headline: MoHUA organises National Conference on Affordable Housing Reforms - “Reimagining Affordable Housing: From Scheme to Sustainable Ecosystem”
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

MoHUA organises National Conference on Affordable Housing Reforms - “Reimagining Affordable Housing: From Scheme to Sustainable Ecosystem”

Land, Rental Housing and Finance at Centre of Affordable Housing Reform Agenda

Shri Rajiv Gauba Calls for Land and Urban Planning Reforms to Boost Affordable Housing

11 AUG 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) organised a National Conference on Affordable Housing Reforms - “Reimagining Affordable Housing: From Scheme to Sustainable Ecosystem” on 11th August 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The Conference brought together senior policymakers, experts and representatives from States/UTs and key financial institutions to deliberate on reforms and innovative approaches for strengthening the affordable housing ecosystem.

The Conference was attended by Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, as Chief Guest, and Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), as the Guest of Honour.

The proceedings began with a welcome address and briefing on housing reforms by Shri Kuldip Narayan, Joint Secretary & Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA), MoHUA. He said that the Conference has been convened to facilitate a focused exchange of experiences, best practices and reform initiatives among States/UTs and to collectively identify practical pathways for implementing reforms that are adaptable to different State contexts.

Addressing the audience, Shri Rajiv Gauba emphasised the need for land and planning reforms to expand affordable housing at scale. He said that land supply and urban planning reforms are critical for expanding affordable housing in cities and stressed the need for measures to improve the availability of land for such projects.

He suggested considering waiving land-use change fees for land dedicated to affordable housing and exempting affordable housing units from stamp duty to improve project viability and affordability.

Shri Rajiv Gauba also highlighted the growing importance of rental housing and stressed the need to expand rental housing for migrant workers, young professionals, students and industrial workers, along with reforms in the tenancy framework.

"Land is the most binding constraint in the housing sector and therefore, it has to be at the centre of the reform agenda," Shri Rajiv Gauba said.

Calling for greater participation of the financial sector, Shri Gauba emphasised the need for financial innovation and increased private capital in affordable housing.

He said the report on affordable housing, prepared by NITI Aayog and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs – “A Comprehensive Framework to Promote Affordable Housing” proposes a set of measures to address the constraints, with most of the implementation lying with State and municipal authorities. The State Government needs a whole-of-government approach to housing, he highlighted.

The recommendations include expanding planned urban areas and reserving at least 10 per cent of residential land as affordable housing zones in master plans. The report also proposes raising the permissible Floor Area Ratio (FAR) for such projects to the range of 5 or 6, promoting transit-oriented development, land pooling and transferable development rights, easing parking and density norms and creating land banks.

The context setting was done by Ms. Anna Roy, Programme Director, Managing Urbanisation, NITI Aayog, who highlighted that affordable housing is fundamental to building inclusive, productive and resilient cities and added that as India's urbanisation gathers pace, the policy approach must evolve from implementing housing schemes to creating a comprehensive ecosystem that continuously supports the supply of affordable housing and expands housing choices for urban households.

Affordable housing requires a supportive ecosystem where land, planning regulations, financing mechanisms, rental markets and institutional arrangements collectively enable the continuous creation of affordable housing. The focus must progressively shift from delivering individual housing projects to creating conditions that make affordable housing viable, accessible and sustainable over the long term, Ms Anna Roy said, citing cities as engines of growth and stressing on the working on the ethos of cooperative federalism.

The Conference provided a platform for stakeholders to deliberate on the need to move beyond a scheme-centric approach towards a sustainable and enabling affordable housing ecosystem, with greater emphasis on policy reforms, institutional convergence, innovative financing mechanisms and effective implementation.

In his keynote speech, Shri Satendra Singh acknowledged the efforts of NITI Aayog and the Committee for the developing a well-researched report “A Comprehensive Framework to Promote Affordable Housing” that adds significant value to ongoing housing and urban development efforts.

He underlined that affordable housing is not merely a social necessity but also a powerful engine for economic growth, employment generation and sustainable urban development. Shri Singh further highlighted how, in the last decade, the Government has fundamentally reshaped the urban housing landscape through Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U).

He mentioned, “The recommendations emerging from this Conference should serve as a roadmap for strengthening affordable housing policies and accelerating India's journey towards sustainable and inclusive urbanisation.”

The deliberations focused on key reforms across land and urban planning, rental housing, vacancy unlocking, access to finance and other areas that can improve housing accessibility and financial viability. The conference aimed to facilitate a shift in the approach to affordable housing to developing a sustainable and integrated ecosystem.

The Conference also highlighted the significant progress made PMAY-U in expanding access to affordable housing and strengthening housing delivery systems across the country. Since its launch in 2015, PMAY-U has supported the construction and delivery of houses for eligible urban families, while promoting women’s ownership, convergence with basic civic amenities and greater participation of States and Urban Local Bodies. Building on these learnings, PMAY-U 2.0 seeks to support 1 crore additional eligible urban families through a demand-driven approach, with emphasis on diverse housing solutions, technology-enabled implementation, access to finance and stronger institutional partnerships. The Conference provided an opportunity to draw upon the experience of PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 while exploring policy and institutional reforms required to create a sustainable, inclusive and financially viable affordable housing ecosystem.

Three technical sessions were hosted during the Conference, covering critical dimensions of affordable housing reforms:

1. Land and Urban Planning Reforms: The session examined State-level experiences and innovative approaches in land and urban planning. Presentations included initiatives from Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Delhi, covering Town Planning models, Affordable Housing Zones, Affordable Housing and Cluster Development Policies and the Delhi Transit-Oriented Development Policy 2026.

2. Expanding Housing Accessibility through Rental Housing and Vacancy Unlock Strategies: The session deliberated on rental housing regulatory reforms and the rental housing exchange, along with experiences and interventions from Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Odisha, Telangana and Assam. The discussions explored approaches to expanding access to affordable rental housing and unlocking existing housing stock.

3. Access to Capital – Demand and Supply Side: Making Affordable Housing Financially Viable: This session focussed on strengthening access to finance for both housing projects and homebuyers. National Housing Bank (NHB) and HUDCO presented initiatives in project finance and home loans. The Department of Financial Services (DFS) and Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) discussed home loan products for persons engaged in the informal sector, while the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) shared insights on the performance of the Credit Guarantee Scheme.

The one-day conference also provided an opportunity for States to showcase their best practices, share experiences and lessons learned and explore approaches that could be adapted and scaled across different urban contexts. The discussions fostered peer learning and cooperative federalism, with participating States sharing their reform initiatives and implementation experiences.

The deliberations will further help in preparing a roadmap for housing sector reforms and share progress made in implementing these reforms. The roadmap is expected to provide a framework for sustained engagement, monitoring of reform measures and exchange of experiences among States. The Conference reaffirmed the importance of collaborative and coordinated efforts among the Centre, States/UTs, financial institutions and other stakeholders to build a more accessible, inclusive and sustainable affordable housing ecosystem.

The National Conference on Affordable Housing Reforms also provided an opportunity to review the progress made by States, learn from successful reform initiatives and collectively identify practical strategies for accelerating implementation under PMAY-U 2.0.

headline: On Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s appeal, members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar to undertake plantation drive across the country on the auspicious occasion of ‘Hariyali Amavasya’; over 50,000 saplings to be planted
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

On Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s appeal, members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar to undertake plantation drive across the country on the auspicious occasion of ‘Hariyali Amavasya’; over 50,000 saplings to be planted

‘Hariyali Amavasya’ is a festival to express gratitude towards nature

Members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar will plant saplings in their villages and cities

Pledge to plant more than 50,000 saplings across the country

Spread the message of environmental conservation among the people along with plantation drive

“Every person should plant at least one sapling on Hariyali Amavasya”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

11 AUG 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will undertake a plantation drive on Wednesday, August 12, on the auspicious occasion of ‘Hariyali Amavasya’, along with hundreds of colleagues at the PBG Ground, Central Range, near Talkatora Stadium in New Delhi. At the same time, thousands of members across the country associated with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Vriksh Mitra Abhiyan will also undertake plantation drives in their respective villages and cities in response to his appeal. On this occasion, a collective pledge has been taken to plant more than 50,000 saplings across the country. The initiative aims to encourage people to celebrate Hariyali Amavasya through active participation in plantation activities and to reinforce the importance of protecting and nurturing the environment. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Abhiyan will participate in the initiative from different parts of the country, taking the message of environmental responsibility to their respective communities and encouraging wider public participation in plantation activities.

Hariyali Amavasya is a festival to express gratitude towards nature

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that August 12 marks the auspicious occasion of Hariyali Amavasya. He said that behind every festival in our country lies a scientific perspective as well as a message aimed at making life better. Hariyali Amavasya is a festival that provides an opportunity to express gratitude towards nature. The greenery spread across the fields and the hope of a new crop arriving fills the mind with happiness and joy. He said that gratitude towards nature should not be expressed merely through words, but should also be demonstrated through action by planting trees. According to Shri Chouhan, the occasion provides an opportunity for people to recognise the importance of nature and contribute towards its protection through meaningful action. Plantation can therefore become a way of expressing appreciation for the natural environment while also encouraging a sense of responsibility towards its conservation. He called upon people to make this festival a celebration of nature through active participation and by adding more greenery to their surroundings.

Thousands of members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar to plant saplings

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar have resolved to celebrate Hariyali Amavasya on August 12 by undertaking plantation drives in their respective villages, cities and panchayats. He said that he himself would also plant saplings in Delhi along with his colleagues on the day. He appealed to the people of the country to make the auspicious occasion of Hariyali Amavasya memorable by planting at least one sapling and contributing towards environmental conservation. He said that the participation of thousands of members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar across the country would help spread the plantation initiative to different communities and locations. By undertaking plantation drives in villages, cities and panchayats, members will not only add greenery to their surroundings but will also carry forward the message of environmental protection and collective responsibility. Shri Chouhan urged citizens to participate in the initiative with enthusiasm and make plantation a meaningful part of the celebration of Hariyali Amavasya.

Every person should plant one sapling

The Union Minister said that planting a sapling is not merely an act of protecting the environment, but also a way of laying the foundation for a safe, secure and beautiful future for generations to come. He appealed to all Vriksh Mitras and citizens across the country to make sure that they plant at least one tree on August 12, on the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya. At the same time, the Union Minister urged people to add five more persons to their plantation pledge and encouraged each of those five people to further involve five persons each, so that the campaign can reach the maximum possible number of people. He said that this chain of participation can help transform plantation into a people’s movement, with individuals encouraging their families, friends, neighbours and wider communities to participate. He also urged citizens to upload information and photographs of their plantation activities on the website shivrajsinghchouhan.co.in, so that the initiative can become a campaign based on the participation of people from all sections of society.

(Release ID: 2297955)

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has called upon members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar to conduct a nationwide plantation drive on August 12, 2026, coinciding with 'Hariyali Amavasya', with a collective pledge to plant over 50,000 saplings across the country to promote environmental conservation.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Date:** August 12, 2026
- **Event:** 'Hariyali Amavasya' plantation drive
- **Lead Organizer:** Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
- **Participants:** Members of Vriksh Mitra Parivar across villages, cities, and panchayats nationwide
- **Location of Main Event:** PBG Ground, Central Range, near Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi
- **Sapling Pledge Target:** More than 50,000 saplings to be planted countrywide
- **Public Appeal:** Citizens encouraged to plant at least one sapling each
- **Expansion Strategy:** Participants urged to involve five additional people, who in turn involve five more each
- **Reporting Mechanism:** Plantation activities to be documented and uploaded on shivrajsinghchouhan.co.in
- **Objective:** Promote environmental responsibility and celebrate Hariyali Amavasya through active tree planting

headline: Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee held in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee held in New Delhi

Bilateral trade rises to USD 592.94 million in 2025-26; investment focal points designated and new Working Groups agreed on services and health

11 AUG 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was held in New Delhi on 10 and 11 August 2026. The Indian delegation was led by Shri Amit Kumar, Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and the Namibian delegation by Ms. Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati, Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade, Government of the Republic of Namibia. The Agreed Minutes of the Session were signed by the two Co-Chairs on 11 August 2026. The inaugural address was delivered by Shri Yashvir Singh, Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce.

Both sides underlined the need to move bilateral trade beyond a raw-material-based composition towards value addition within Namibia, and to translate discussions into concrete mechanisms with defined timelines and assigned responsibilities.

Trade performance: Bilateral merchandise trade rose to USD 592.94 million in 2025-26 from USD 568.40 million in 2024-25, with India's exports at USD 349.09 million and imports at USD 243.85 million. Trade in services grew by 7.34 per cent to USD 380 million in calendar year 2024.

Sectoral growth: India's engineering exports grew by 124.06 per cent to USD 30.24 million, led by motor vehicles and components. Exports of pharmaceuticals and medical devices reached USD 36.50 million, India being Namibia's second-largest pharmaceutical source with a 16.4 per cent share.

Investment focal points: Invest India and the Namibia Investment Promotion and Development Board designated as JTC investment focal points, with a named official on each side.

Services Working Group: A dedicated Services Working Group to be constituted, meeting no later than February 2027 and submitting its work plan to the JTC.

Health and pharmaceuticals: First Joint Working Group under the Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the Field of Health and Medicine to be convened by December 2026; the Janaushadhi cooperation agreement with HLL Lifecare Limited at an advanced stage of finalisation.

Critical minerals: Structured cooperation identified across exploration, offtake, processing and downstream beneficiation in lithium, graphite, copper, cobalt and rare earth elements, in line with Namibia's priorities of value addition and local employment creation.

Gems and jewellery: Namibian participation invited in India's Special Notified Zones at Surat and Mumbai and in the India Rough Gemstones Sourcing Show, together with training support in diamond cutting, polishing and jewellery design.

Digital cooperation: Continued rollout of the instant payment system built on India's Unified Payments Interface, unveiled in Namibia as “WayaMe” on 15 June 2026, with proposals for a FinTech Cooperation Framework between the Reserve Bank of India and the Bank of Namibia.

Energy and infrastructure: Cooperation identified in railways and rolling stock, solar and wind power, battery storage, transmission, green hydrogen, biofuels and desalination.

India-SACU PTA: Terms of Reference finalised and scheduled for signature on 12 August 2026, with negotiations to commence within one month of signature and to conclude within one year.

The Joint Trade Committee is the principal bilateral institutional mechanism for reviewing trade, investment and economic cooperation between the two countries. Cooperation was also taken forward at the Session in agriculture and food security, MSMEs, textiles, tourism and sports. The discussions were held in a friendly and cordial atmosphere, reflecting the traditional bonds of friendship between the two countries. The Fifth Session of the JTC will be held in Namibia in 2028 on dates to be mutually agreed through diplomatic channels.

Abhishek Dayal/Abhijith Narayanan

headline: Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala to Roll Out First Rake of LHB Coaches for Bangladesh Railway
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala to Roll Out First Rake of LHB Coaches for Bangladesh Railway

11 AUG 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi

Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala, is set to achieve another significant milestone with the rollout of the first rake comprising 19 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches for Bangladesh Railway on 12 August 2026.

The first rake comprises 03 AC Sleeper Cars, 03 AC Chair Cars, 11 Non-AC Chair Cars and 02 Power Cars. These coaches incorporate several unique design features and modifications, many of which have been developed for the first time in LHB-type coaches.

The coaches have been specially customised to meet the operational and passenger requirements of Bangladesh Railway. The seating arrangement incorporates specially designed reclining chairs with stainless steel armrests and stainless steel footrests, offering multiple reclining positions for enhanced passenger comfort. The coaches are equipped with a number of passenger-centric features, including fans in AC coaches, an integrated CCTV surveillance system, a passenger alarm system, partially openable windows, a Baby Care Room and a Prayer Room. Considering the specific operating conditions, the roof structure has been strengthened to withstand additional loading arising from passengers travelling on the roof during peak traffic periods.

A major technological feature is the incorporation of crashworthy design provisions complying with European Standard EN 15227. This required a comprehensive redesign of the car body shell to enhance collision performance and passenger safety. The electrical system of these coaches has also been specially designed for 415 V operation, as against the conventional 750 V system used in Indian Railways coaches.

The association between RCF and Bangladesh Railway began with the successful supply of 120 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches during 2015-16. Building upon this successful partnership, Bangladesh Railway once again entrusted RCF, through RITES, with a prestigious order in 2024 for the manufacture and supply of 200 broad gauge passenger coaches in seven variants.

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Manik Sharma

headline: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways Approves ₹334.89 Crore Flyover at Visakhapatnam Port to Ease Cargo Movement
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways Approves ₹334.89 Crore Flyover at Visakhapatnam Port to Ease Cargo Movement

3.584-km elevated corridor from Convent Junction to Dock Area to separate road and rail traffic, remove bottlenecks at nine level crossings

11 AUG 2026 8:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has approved a ₹334.89-crore internal flyover at Visakhapatnam Port Authority to improve cargo evacuation, reduce traffic congestion and streamline movement within the port premises.

The project, approved by Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal, was appraised by the Delegated Investment Board (DIB) chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

On the occasion, Sarbananda Sonowal said, “This project will remove a critical bottleneck at Visakhapatnam Port, enabling faster cargo movement and improving overall operational efficiency. We are committed to building modern, seamless and globally competitive port infrastructure under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.”

The proposed 3.584-km elevated corridor, connecting Convent Junction with the Dock Area, will separate road and rail traffic within the port. The project is aimed at addressing delays at nine major railway level crossings, which currently see about 18 gate closures a day due to high train exchange volumes.

The frequent closures contribute to congestion, longer vehicle waiting times, higher fuel consumption and increased vehicle operating costs, affecting the efficiency of cargo evacuation. By providing an elevated road corridor, the project will enable smoother movement of vehicles and cargo while reducing conflicts between road and rail traffic. The project will include associated civil and electrical works, utility shifting, safety installations and five years of maintenance. Construction will be planned to minimise disruption to ongoing port operations, particularly in critical dock areas.

Speaking on the occasion, Sarbananda Sonowal said, “Prime Minister Narendra Modi has transformed India’s maritime sector into a key driver of economic growth, self-reliance and national development. With stronger infrastructure, progressive reforms, modern technology and greater investment in our maritime capabilities, we are building a globally competitive and self-reliant maritime ecosystem that will power India’s journey towards an Atmanirbhar Bharat and a Viksit Bharat 2047.”

The investment is aligned with the Government's broader focus on integrated infrastructure planning under the PM GatiShakti framework. By improving last-mile connectivity within the port and facilitating faster cargo evacuation, the elevated corridor is expected to strengthen Visakhapatnam Port's role in India's maritime logistics and trade network.

The project is scheduled for completion within 30 months of commencement.

headline: Union Health Minister, Shri J P Nadda, chairs a discussion with MPs from Karnataka and Keralam providing impetus to efforts toward TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister, Shri J P Nadda, chairs a discussion with MPs from Karnataka and Keralam providing impetus to efforts toward TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan

Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs from Karnataka and Keralam reinforce their commitments to create a TB-Mukt Karnataka and Keralam and TB-Mukt Bharat

Union Minister provides MPs with specific oversight checkpoints to engage with District Collectors and health facilities; calls for intensified and active engagement from parliamentarians

Shri Nadda highlights innovative case-finding strategies and patient-centric care as cornerstones of India’s TB elimination strategy, propelling the country’s progress ahead of high-burden countries

MPs commit to generate greater awareness, provide supportive supervision to ensure quality services and mobilize communities into a Jan Andolan for a TB Mukt Bharat

11 AUG 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda met Members of Parliament (MPs) from Karnataka and Keralam today on the sidelines of the Monsoon Session of Parliament. He was also joined by Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister of Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy; Smt. Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare & Chemicals and Fertilizers; Shri Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas and Tourism; Smt. Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME and MoS for Labour and Employment along with other parliamentarians.

The meeting, titled "Parliamentarians Championing a TB Mukt Bharat," brought together Members of Parliament from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha from Karnataka and Keralam across party lines at the Extended Parliament House Annexe underscoring a unified political resolve to accelerate progress towards a TB-free India. The meeting was part of a series of sensitisation interactions chaired by the Union Health Minister with Members of Parliament from states across the country, including West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and others. Shri Nadda informed the Members that similar consultations have been held with MPs from other States as well, as part of the Government's whole-of-government approach to accelerate TB elimination.

The meeting reviewed the progress made under the 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented in two phases to accelerate India's efforts towards TB elimination. The first phase, launched on 7th December 2024, initially covered 347 high-priority districts before being expanded nationwide and concluded on 24th March 2025. The second phase, launched on 24th March 2026 and recently concluded in July focused on nearly 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and urban wards across the country. The meeting looked at the progress of TB activities in the state and UTs, and discussed the way forward.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda described the campaign as “a defining moment in the nation’s fight against tuberculosis, built on innovation, compassion and unwavering political will.” He highlighted India's accelerated gains in TB elimination on the global stage. He noted that “the country has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024, nearly twice the global pace, and has achieved a treatment coverage rate of 92%, as per the WHO Global TB Report 2025.” Shri Nadda underlined that expanding outreach in screening, treatment, and patient support in Karnataka and Keralam will be critical in translating national momentum into community-level impact.

The Union Minister highlighted the remarkable success of the recently concluded 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, which ran from March 24 to July 4, 2026. The campaign screened over 2.02 crore vulnerable individuals across the country and detected over 7 lakh new TB cases, including 1.97 lakh asymptomatic cases who would have otherwise remained undetected. Emphasizing the decisive role of political leadership, Shri Nadda called upon parliamentarians to anchor TB elimination efforts in their constituencies through sustained public engagement, administrative oversight, and social mobilization. He noted that “TB Mukt Bharat is not merely a health programme, but a people’s movement driven by collective ownership.”

In his concluding remarks, Shri Nadda commended the parliamentarians for their commitment and expressed confidence in the state’s potential to lead. He observed that the close of the 100-day campaign marks not the end of responsibility but the point at which deeper, sustained work begins, and that the programme’s success would be measured by consistent progress in every district.

Placing their efforts in context, the Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava shared that Karnataka and Keralam, which have vulnerable factors like urban settings, migrant population, urban slums, traditional health-seeking behaviour, under-nutrition, alcohol/tobacco use, high burden of HIV & diabetes, elderly population with comorbidities, construction & industrial workforce, hilly & tribal areas, stone quarries, silk weavers, workers in coffee estate & tea plantations workers, carry a high burden of TB.

The Additional Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik highlighted the technological foundation that has powered the campaign, noting that India has scaled molecular testing from a few hundred machines a decade ago to over 11,000 today, supported by nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units in the field, built on homegrown innovation to ensure that no patient is left behind. She presented a snapshot of Karnataka and Keralam’s performance across key indicators such as TB notifications, treatment success, preventive treatment coverage, and alignment with national elimination benchmarks. She noted that during the 100-day campaign, the two states devised specific strategies taking Ayushman Arogya Shivirs directly into urban slums, construction sites and migrant clusters to bring screening and care closer to those who need them most.

The MPs from Karnataka and Keralam, present in the meeting reaffirmed their commitment to intensify awareness campaigns, stigma reduction efforts, and Ni-kshay Shivirs to promote early detection, especially among vulnerable groups, irrespective of whether they display any symptoms of TB or not. The parliamentarians will also be strengthening oversight of TB services at district and block levels to ensure quality diagnostics and patient-centric care are available at the last mile. Building on the efforts under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, they will continue leading Jan Andolan to mobilise communities to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood assistance to those affected by TB.

LAUNCH OF NEXT GENERATION OFFSHORE PATROL VESSEL

(YARD 3037, SHRUTI) AT M/s GRSE, KOLKATA

11 AUG 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

Yard 3037 (Shruti), Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (NGOPV), was launched at M/s GRSE, Kolkata on 11 Aug 2026 by Mrs Manika Sadhu, in the presence of Vice Admiral Sanjay Sadhu, Controller of Warship Production & Acquisition. The event reflected the rich traditions, and ethos of the Indian Navy. Senior dignitaries from the Indian Navy, Ministry of Defence, and GRSE attended the occasion.

The construction of NGOPVs is concurrently being undertaken at two shipyards (GSL, Goa & GRSE, Kolkata). These indigenously designed and built ships will augment the existing OPVs/ NOPVs for multi domain operations, such as maritime surveillance, search and rescue, protection of offshore assets, HADR and anti-piracy missions. These ships derive their name from India’s rich heritage, with this ship being named as ‘Shruti’, referring to four Vedas. The crest design of the ship depicts the constellation of Ursa Major and a red & white coloured light house.

The launch marks yet another significant milestone in Indian Navy’s pursuit towards indigenous shipbuilding and is in consonance with Government of India’s vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Make in India’ initiative.

headline: PRESS RELEASE ON 392nd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
fullText:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat

PRESS RELEASE ON 392nd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE

11 AUG 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture headed by Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha, M.P., Rajya Sabha, presented its 392nd Report on “Enabling Inclusive, Digital and Sustainable Bus Transport: Policy, Regulation and Public-Private Partnership for Next-Gen Mobility” on Tuesday, the 11th August, 2026.

The Report was adopted by the Committee on 6th August, 2026. The Key Recommendations/Observations made by the Committee in this Report are enclosed.

The full Report is available on the website of Rajya Sabha https://sansad.in/rs -→Committees→Department related RS→Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture-→ Report

THE THREE HUNDRED NINETY SECOND REPORT OF MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

KEY HIGHLIGHTS OF THE COMMITTEE’S

RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE — AT A GLANCE

1. All India Passenger Permit:- Replace the All India Tourist Permit, within one year, with an All India Passenger Permit issued by the State of first registration, its rights stated exhaustively on its face; enforce it exclusively through electronic correlation of VAHAN, FASTag and vehicle location data, commission the monitoring centres, end the border check posts in the six States where they persist, and, with the insurance regulator, place the injured passenger's claim beyond dispute. (Paras 4.2 to 4.5)

2. National Bus Terminals Authority:- Separate terminal ownership from bus operation as settled national policy; constitute a dedicated terminals authority on the Airports Authority model; circulate a non-discriminatory access framework on the Kashmere Gate template; frame a National Code for Bus Terminals within one year; pursue Gurugram and Katra as templates; notify the standard bus stop and circulate it to Members of Parliament for MPLADS funding. (Paras 4.6 to 4.9)

3. National Bus Digital Grid:- Notify interoperability standards within one year; upon them, a public live-tracking layer aligned with Indian Railways specifications, unified booking across public and private operators, a moderated crowdsourced rating system linked to the permit databases, a cVIGIL-pattern citizen vigilance channel with geo-tagged, time-bound reporting of bus and terminal conditions, and a GIS-based network atlas from vehicle tracking and toll data publishing punctuality and predictability metrics and hazard maps; participation phased and mandatory for commercial permit holders; a measurable programme of work for the digital pillar within six months. (Paras 4.10 to 4.13)

4. Operator-centric safety:- A district-wise completion plan for Automated Testing Stations within six months; verification of fire, egress and alert equipment at every fitness test so that life-safety standards reach the fleet in service; retro-fitment examined for sleeper and school buses; a published operator safety rating taken into account at permit renewal; and the emergency alert system made to function within one year, failing which the levy upon operators for it shall cease. (Paras 4.14 to 4.17)

5. Fleet Transition Compact:- Fleet-ownership and leasing entities so operators run buses they need not own, entered through scrap-and-lease at registered scrapping facilities; review of the private scrapping incentive; a time-bound plan for electric buses, with a target for each operator and buses bought in bulk on standard terms; charging matched to where buses operate; an end-of-life framework for electric buses and batteries within one year; regional manufacturing, testing and maintenance clusters. (Paras 4.18 to 4.21)

6. Services for women, run by women:- A reported programme, within six months, of dedicated peak-hour services operated with women bus drivers and women staff; CCTV in new buses brought into force; the alert-system programme completed beyond sixteen States; on-board toilet standardisation concluded under the Bus Body Code; monitored sanitation at overnight halts; funding on a common footing such as an Inclusive Transport Fund. (Paras 4.22 to 4.25)

7. National Tourist Bus Grid:- Integrated tourist circuits interconnecting bus, rail, metro, air and waterways with unified ticketing; a centralized accredited Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul system with digital logbooks for the tourist fleet; intermodal hubs at major destinations on the Katra template with revenue-sharing between public and private participants; tourist-facing terminal standards and published satisfaction surveys. (Paras 4.26 to 4.29)

8. A budgetary identity for the bus passenger:- A defined provision for public transport infrastructure within the Ministry's budget, reported within six months, with the Ministry's considered position on applying a proportion of the order of 25 per cent of the road allocation to it; viability gap funding for conforming terminals and testing stations; MPLADS circulation of the standard bus stop within three months of notification. (Paras 4.30 to 4.32)

9. The State of the States:- An annual published ranking of States on bus transport facilitation, on verifiable parameters from testing density to terminal access to the functioning of emergency systems and the punctuality metrics of the network atlas, with operator and passenger feedback including the disposal record of citizen vigilance reports; the first edition to disclose the identity of the States still operating border check posts. (Paras 4.33 to 4.35)

10. Count the passenger:- Reconciliation of the fleet figures within six months, with Telangana's integration into VAHAN pursued and disclosed meanwhile; a consolidated all-category statement of buses; a federated national data architecture in which the States own their systems; and a periodic authoritative estimate of passengers carried by bus, published with the authority accorded to the statistics of other modes. (Paras 4.36 to 4.38)

(Release ID: 2297871)

headline: Investigation into Air India Flight AI 2379 (Phuket–Delhi) of 04.08.2026
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Investigation into Air India Flight AI 2379 (Phuket–Delhi) of 04.08.2026

11 AUG 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

On 04.08.2026, an Air India Airbus A320 aircraft, registration VT-EXO, operating scheduled flight AI 2379 from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a sudden altitude variation of approximately 300 feet during cruise. The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely at Delhi.

During the occurrence, injuries were reported to 20 passengers and four cabin crew members. The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members comprising two pilots and six cabin crew.

Based on the information received from DGCA and the nature of the occurrence, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has taken up the investigation in accordance with the applicable provisions and ICAO protocols. The requisite notifications have been made to ICAO and the concerned States.

The participation of the State of Design and the State of Manufacture in an aircraft incident of such nature is an established part of the international investigation framework prescribed under ICAO protocols.

Accordingly, the Bureau d’Enquêtes et d’Analyses pour la sécurité de l’aviation civile (BEA), France, as the investigation authority of the concerned State, along with technical representatives of Airbus, is extending the necessary technical assistance to AAIB, including provision of relevant technical information and design documentation, in accordance with the applicable ICAO framework.

AAIB is presently engaged in the systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidences. This includes examination of the aircraft and its systems, recorded flight data, relevant operational and maintenance records, medical information, and interviews with persons concerned. All material evidence will be examined in its entirety before any conclusions are drawn.

The sole objective of the investigation is to determine the circumstances and contributing factors relating to the occurrence and to identify appropriate safety measures to prevent recurrence. The investigation is independent, evidence-based and comprehensive, and no inference regarding the cause of the occurrence should be drawn from any isolated piece of information while the investigation is in progress.

Certain records, statements, medical information and other material collected during the investigation are protected and confidential in accordance with the applicable investigation framework. Maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of the investigation process is essential to a fair, objective and technically sound determination of the facts. The AAIB therefore requests all concerned, including the media and the public, to respect the investigation process and refrain from drawing conclusions on the basis of incomplete, unverified or selectively available information.

The AAIB will conduct a thorough investigation covering all material facts and relevant evidence and will issue its preliminary findings within the stipulated timeframe in accordance with the applicable provisions and ICAO protocols. Further information will be placed in the public domain at the appropriate stage of the investigation.

The AAIB remains committed to an independent, transparent and professional investigation, with aviation safety as its overriding objective.

(Release ID: 2297850)

headline: Government Strengthens Access to National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SC Students
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Access to National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SC Students

580 Students Awarded Scholarships and Enrolled Abroad Under the Scheme from 2019-20 to 2025-26

11 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has stated that a total of 580 students have been awarded scholarships and enrolled abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme for Scheduled Castes during the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 (till August 6, 2026).

The written reply was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in response to Shri Daggumalla Prasada Rao in the Lok Sabha.

According to the information furnished by the Ministry, 41 students received scholarships in 2019-20, followed by 71 in 2020-21, 98 in 2021-22, 98 in 2022-23, 114 in 2023-24, 80 in 2024-25 and 78 in 2025-26.

To raise awareness about the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme among students, relevant details including scheme guidelines and instructions are posted on the Departmental website.

The Minister further submitted that advertisements are also published in newspapers and letters are sent to the Social Welfare Departments of State Governments and Union Territories with a request for widespread publicity of the Scheme.

Applications under the NOS Scheme are invited through the online portal. The Scheme has recently been onboarded to the newly launched unified SAMAVESH (Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony) Portal, to streamline application processing, scrutiny, data management, accessibility and the selection process.

Under the NOS Scheme, funds are released in advance through Letters of Authorization (LoA) to the concerned Indian Missions/Embassies with direction to disburse the requisite funds to concerned Universities and students at the earliest upon receipt of claims.

In Andhra Pradesh, 18 students have been awarded scholarships and enrolled abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme during the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26. The number of beneficiaries was 4 in 2020-21, 3 in 2023-24, 3 in 2024-25 and 5 in 2025-26.

District-wise data for Andhra Pradesh shows that students from Chittoor received scholarships in 2020-21, 2023-24 and 2025-26. Beneficiaries were also recorded from Annamayya, Bapatla, Krishna, Palnadu, Prakasam, Visakhapatnam and Y.S.R. Kadapa districts during the period.

The Government's measures to expand awareness, digitise the application process and facilitate timely disbursement are aimed at improving access to overseas higher education opportunities for Scheduled Caste students.

headline: Central Government Disburses ₹19,216.46 Crore Under Various Scholarship Schemes for SC Students During Last Three Years
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Central Government Disburses ₹19,216.46 Crore Under Various Scholarship Schemes for SC Students During Last Three Years

Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students Accounts for ₹17,224.63 Crore; DBT and Regular Reviews Help Streamline Scholarship Disbursement

11 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has disbursed a total of ₹19,216.46 crore during the last three financial years towards various scholarship schemes for Scheduled Caste (SC) students administered by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

This information was provided by the Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar in a reply to Shri Raja A in the Lok Sabha today.

He said the total amount disbursed under these scholarship schemes increased from ₹6,094.48 crore in 2023-24 to ₹6,200.59 crore in 2024-25 and further to ₹6,921.39 crore in 2025-26.

The scholarship schemes covered include the Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others, Top Class Education Scheme (TCS) and the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme for SC and other eligible candidates, he further said.

Dr Kumar said under the Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students, ₹17,224.63 crore was disbursed during the last three financial years. The amount released increased from ₹5,475.42 crore in 2023-24 to ₹5,562.26 crore in 2024-25 and ₹6,186.95 crore in 2025-26.

The Minister further said the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others accounted for ₹1,469.92 crore during the three-year period, with ₹446.66 crore released in 2023-24, ₹460.90 crore in 2024-25 and ₹562.36 crore in 2025-26. Under the Top Class Education Scheme, ₹304.29 crore was released, while ₹217.62 crore was released under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme during the same period.

Under the Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students, Tamil Nadu received ₹713.70 crore in 2023-24, ₹1,032.09 crore in 2024-25 and ₹1,034.94 crore in 2025-26 as Central Assistance. Maharashtra received ₹1,652.98 crore, ₹929.92 crore and ₹1,095.80 crore respectively during the three years, while Uttar Pradesh received ₹674.83 crore, ₹366.02 crore and ₹617.64 crore respectively.

Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others, Tamil Nadu received ₹70.56 crore in 2023-24, ₹109.45 crore in 2024-25 and ₹121.49 crore in 2025-26.

The Post Matric Scholarship for SCs and Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs & Others are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, under which the Department releases the Central share through the central portal after the respective States and Union Territories release their share. The National Overseas Scholarship and Top Class Education Scheme for SCs are Central Sector Schemes.

Under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme, funds are released in advance through a Letter of Authorisation (LoA) to Indian Missions, while funds under the Top Class Education Scheme are released directly to eligible students through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

The Minister stated that Department regularly reviews the scholarship schemes to address issues relating to delayed release of scholarships. Measures include capacity-building programmes, technical handholding, national-level Chintan Shivirs and workshops involving States, Union Territories and other stakeholders.

The Government has further stated that DBT into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries has streamlined payment processes and reduced delays.

Under the Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers for Scheduled Castes (SHREYAS-SCs), the Top Class Scholarship for SC Students is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme and, therefore, there is no State-wise or district-wise allocation. During the last three financial years, ₹304.29 crore was released under the scheme.

The Government continues to strengthen the implementation of scholarship schemes through digital payment mechanisms, regular reviews, technical support and capacity-building initiatives to facilitate timely release of scholarships to eligible SC students across the country.

headline: Government Strengthens Rehabilitation Framework for Persons Engaged in Begging under SMILE-Beggary Scheme
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Rehabilitation Framework for Persons Engaged in Begging under SMILE-Beggary Scheme

₹45.59 Crore Released under SMILE-Beggary Scheme Since Inception; 10,446 Persons Including 2,824 Children Rehabilitated

11 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has taken comprehensive measures to strengthen the care, rehabilitation and social reintegration of persons engaged in begging through the Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging (SMILE-Beggary) Scheme.

This information was provided by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma, in a written reply to Dr. M P Abdussamad Samdani in the Lok Sabha.

The reply said that since inception of the SMILE-Beggary Scheme on 23 October 2023 and up to 31 July 2026, a total of ₹45.59 crore has been released under the Scheme. This includes ₹40.04 crore released to implementing authorities/cities, with the balance utilised towards administrative and other scheme-related expenditure.

As on 31 July 2026, a total of 10,446 persons including 2,824 children, have been rehabilitated under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme. Of these, 7,622 are adult beneficiaries, the reply further said.

Children rescued under the Scheme are provided age-appropriate care, education, counselling and family reintegration and are therefore not covered under vocational training interventions.

The Scheme provides vocational training to eligible beneficiaries based on their aptitude, age, physical and mental condition, and local livelihood opportunities. Training includes trades and livelihood activities such as carpentry, tailoring, housekeeping, management of community toilets, sanitation services, hair cutting, security services, cooking, gardening, driving/operation of e-rickshaws and other locally relevant trades.

Beneficiaries are also facilitated in forming community/group-based Self-Help Groups and are linked with banks and other financial institutions for financial assistance to undertake self-employment and income-generating activities. These include tiffin stalls/food vending carts, vegetable vending carts and group-based enterprises such as preparation of spices, pickles, snacks and papads.

The written reply said as per the State/UT-wise details provided in the Lok Sabha reply, Tamil Nadu recorded the highest number of adult beneficiaries rehabilitated at 1,557, followed by Madhya Pradesh (1,135), Uttar Pradesh (884), Maharashtra (817), Assam (472), Andhra Pradesh (466), Jammu & Kashmir (434) and Kerala (418).

The Government's measures under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme aim to strengthen institutional mechanisms for care, rehabilitation, skill development, livelihood support and social reintegration, while ensuring dignified living conditions and effective monitoring of Beggars’/Shelter Homes.

In compliance with the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in M.S. Patter vs. State of NCT of Delhi (Civil Appeal No. 12216 of 2025), the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has developed Model Guidelines for Beggars’/Shelter Homes through a National Consultative Committee and extensive consultations with States and Union Territories. The Guidelines were circulated to all States/UTs on 13 April 2026 for necessary compliance and effective implementation.

The National Consultative Committee included representatives from the Ministries of Law & Justice, Health & Family Welfare, Housing and Urban Affairs, Women and Child Development, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, the National Human Rights Commission, State/UT Governments and non-governmental organisations working in the sector.

The Model Guidelines establish a comprehensive framework for humane, dignified and rights-based rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging. They prescribe minimum standards for infrastructure and capacity, preventive healthcare and sanitation, nutrition and food safety, vocational training and rehabilitation, legal aid and awareness, child and gender sensitivity, accountability, oversight, monitoring, implementation and compliance.

To facilitate identification, profiling and rehabilitation, the Ministry has developed a dedicated mobile application, with login credentials shared with implementing cities. The application facilitates a comprehensive survey of persons engaged in begging for their rehabilitation under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme.

The Model Guidelines further provide for establishment of a Digital Monitoring System by States/UTs to capture standardised information relating to admission of rescued persons/residents, health status, skill development and training, rehabilitation, release, follow-up and family reunion. The National Online Portal of the Ministry serves as a central repository of information relating to the SMILE-Beggary Scheme and facilitates real-time monitoring of implementation across States and Union Territories through periodic reporting and maintenance of scheme-related information.

Two-Yearly Infrastructure and Social Audits

The Model Guidelines mandate that every Beggar/Shelter Home undergo a third-party infrastructure and social audit at least once every two years. The audit covers structural safety, disability and age-friendliness, electrical systems, sanitation, water supply, and the safety and security of residents. The District Social Welfare Officer or designated authority is responsible for monitoring compliance and ensuring timely rectification of deficiencies identified during the audit. The Guidelines also prescribe minimum space standards for Beggars’/Shelter Homes to prevent overcrowding and ensure dignified living conditions.

(Release ID: 2297830)

### OVERVIEW  
The Central Government has implemented the SMILE-Beggary Scheme to rehabilitate persons engaged in begging through financial allocation, vocational training, and institutional framework improvements, with ₹45.59 crore disbursed and over 10,000 beneficiaries rehabilitated as of July 2026.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Funding**: ₹45.59 crore released since 23 October 2023 (₹40.04 crore to implementing authorities, balance for administrative costs).  
- **Rehabilitation**: 10,446 persons (2,824 children, 7,622 adults) rehabilitated under the scheme.  
- **Vocational Training**: Includes carpentry, tailoring, e-rickshaw operation, and group enterprises (e.g., food vending, spice preparation).  
- **State-LevelPerformance**: Tamil Nadu led with 1,557 adult recipients; other top states included Madhya Pradesh (1,135) and Uttar Pradesh (884).  
- **Model Guidelines**: Developed post-Supreme Court direction (M.S. Patter case), establishing standards for shelter homes, healthcare, training, and dignity.  
- **Digital Tools**: Mobile app for beneficiary identification and a national online portal for real-time monitoring.  
- **Audits**: Mandatory third-party infrastructure and social audits every two years for shelter homes.  
- **Implementation Framework**: Involves National Consultative Committee (cross-ministerial and NGO representatives) and state-level compliance mechanisms.

headline: CCRAS-CARI Inaugurates Extension OPD Facility in New Delhi
fullText:
CCRAS-CARI Inaugurates Extension OPD Facility in New Delhi

New Facility to Expand Access to Quality, Evidence-Based Ayurvedic Healthcare Services in the National Capital

11 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), New Delhi, under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Ministry of Ayush today inaugurated an Extension Outpatient Department (OPD) in New Delhi. The new facility is aimed at further strengthening the delivery of accessible, quality and evidence-based Ayurvedic healthcare services to the people of Rohini and adjoining areas.

Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, inaugurated the facility in the presence of senior officers and dignitaries.

Addressing the gathering, Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya reiterated CCRAS’s commitment to expanding the reach of evidence-based Ayurveda and making quality Ayurvedic healthcare services more accessible to the public. He emphasised the importance of strengthening clinical services and extending the benefits of Ayurveda to communities through institutional and outreach initiatives.

Dr. Hemanta Panigrahi, Institute In-charge, CARI, delivered the welcome address, while Dr. N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, CCRAS, highlighted the importance of expanding evidence-based Ayurvedic clinical services at the community level. Shri Deepak Kochhar, Deputy Director (Administration), CCRAS, and Shri M. Shivkumar Reddy, Superintendent Engineer, CPWD, spoke on the administrative and infrastructure aspects of the facility.

The new Extension OPD will provide accessible Ayurvedic outpatient services to residents of Rohini and adjoining areas, strengthening CARI, New Delhi’s clinical outreach and bringing evidence-based Ayurveda closer to the community.

The initiative is in line with the Ministry of Ayush’s continued efforts to strengthen the Ayush healthcare ecosystem, expand institutional healthcare infrastructure and make traditional systems of medicine more accessible to citizens. Such outreach facilities also support the broader objective of integrating evidence-based practices of Ayurveda into accessible and community-oriented healthcare delivery.

The inauguration marks another step towards strengthening the network of Ayurvedic clinical services in the National Capital and advancing the vision of accessible, quality and evidence-based Ayush healthcare for all.

Extension OPD Facility Address: FC-5, Block-A, Sector-28, Rohini, New Delhi.

GeM has started utilising AI/ML based analytical models to identify suspicious procurement patterns, including potential buyer-seller collusion, abnormal pricing and repeated participation patterns. These models help in identifying cases pertaining to Order Splitting, suspected Buyer Seller Collusion based on the similar digital footprints, Bidder's qualification ratio, procurement prices vis-a-vis product median prices etc. The cases flagged through these analytical tools are made accessible to the concerned authorities within the buyer organizations for further review and necessary action.

GeM tries to leverage upon the Competition Commission of India (CCI) toolkit to identify any suspected cartels, based on the bidder's digital footprints, like IP address, bid pricing, submission timings etc. GeM has established an Incident Management framework under which violations relating to submission of false documents, fraudulent practices, collusive behaviour and other misconduct are examined and appropriate administrative action, including suspension, and other measures as per GeM policies, are regularly taken.

2024-25 | 1,96,803 | 62,091

2025-26 | 1,81,035 | 55,772

The main reasons for suspension include:

Listing the products/services in wrong category or with wrong specifications.

Unreasonable offer price

Delay in Delivery as per contract

Refuses to supply products/services after placement of contract.

GeM has implemented multiple safeguards to strengthen vendor verification and procurement integrity, including the following:

GeM has a fully online vendor registration process.

GeM has deployed advanced analytics tools to detect procurement anomalies such as order splitting, suspicious bidding, abnormal pricing and potential collusion, with flagged cases reflected on primary buyer's dashboards for action.

Anti-competitive behaviour or cartel formation is classified as a Severe/Grave deviation under GeM's Incident Management framework, with proven cases attracting suspension of up to 365 days.

This information was given by Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: From Financial Constraints to Educational Confidence: How Scholarship Support Helped YELUKURU SUDEEKSHA Continue Her B.Tech. Education
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Constraints to Educational Confidence: How Scholarship Support Helped YELUKURU SUDEEKSHA Continue Her B.Tech. Education

11 AUG 2026 11:45PM by PIB Delhi

Access to quality education can play an important role in helping students pursue their aspirations and build better opportunities for the future. However, for students from families with limited incomes, financial difficulties can become a major challenge in meeting college expenses and continuing higher education.

Demonstrating how scholarship assistance can provide relief to students facing economic challenges, Ms Yelukuru Sudeeksha, an 18-year-old student belonging to the Other Backward Class (OBC) category, is pursuing her second year of B.Tech. education. Coming from a middle-class family, she faced difficulties in managing her college fees regularly as her father had to meet household and family expenses with a limited income. Paying the entire fee amount at once was a major challenge, creating financial pressure and uncertainty for the family. Despite these difficulties, Sudeeksha remained determined to complete her education successfully and work towards a stable and respectable career.

In 2025-26, scholarship assistance of ₹4,85,000 was provided to Sudeeksha. The support helped her pay her college fees independently without completely depending on her parents for financial support. It reduced the financial burden on her family and enabled her to continue her education with greater confidence and focus on her academic goals.

With the financial burden related to her college fees reduced, Sudeeksha has been able to continue her B.Tech. education with greater confidence. The scholarship support has helped address an important financial challenge and allowed her to concentrate on her studies while working towards her career aspirations.

Sudeeksha's story highlights how timely scholarship assistance can provide meaningful support to students facing financial constraints. By reducing the pressure of educational expenses, the support has enabled her to continue her higher education and pursue her aspiration of securing a good job with a stable and respectable salary package, so that she can support her family financially and contribute towards improving their overall living conditions.

### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, on behalf of hon'ble PM, launched the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA) / Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October 2024. The Abhiyan comprises 25 interventions by 17 ministries to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, improve access to health, education, Anganwadi facilities, and provide livelihood opportunities, benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in a 5-year period.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Launch:** 2nd October 2024.
- **Interventions:** 25 by 17 ministries.
- **Overall Targets:** Saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages; benefit >5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks across 30 States/UTs within 5 years (2024-2028).

  - PMAY-G Housing (MoRD): 13,02,811 houses sanctioned; 8,21,566 completed.
  - PMGSY Roads (MoRD): 5,008 km roads sanctioned in 14 states; 3.9 km road work completed.

headline: “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

“DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”

12 AUG 2026 12:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that currently, the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has reduced processing time and reduced grievances. The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at Annexure-I.

The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are given as under: -

End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals.

Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of the Ministry

Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and administrative delays.

Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome tracking.

The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and databases.

Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate parking of funds at State level, minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of scholarship.

Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of intermediaries.
