headline: India Reaffirms Commitment to Elephant Conservation on World Elephant Day 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India Reaffirms Commitment to Elephant Conservation on World Elephant Day 2026

Securing the Future of Elephants Means Securing Our Forests, Biodiversity and Ecological Heritage: Shri Bhupender Yadav

12 AUG 2026 11:19AM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of World Elephant Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, reaffirmed India’s commitment to securing a shared future for elephants and people.

In a post on social media, the Minister noted that India has 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 States and 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors. Shri Yadav said advanced population monitoring and stronger measures would mitigate human-elephant conflict are strengthening elephant conservation.

On #WorldElephantDay, we reaffirm India’s commitment to securing a shared future for elephants and people.

With 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 States, 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors, advanced population monitoring and stronger measures to mitigate human-elephant… pic.twitter.com/jIdd1PXHMH

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) August 12, 2026

The Minister further stated, “when we secure the future of elephants, we secure our forests, biodiversity and ecological heritage”. The Minister called for an action to ensure that the elephant continues to walk freely through India’s forests and landscapes for generations to come.

On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that India is home to one of the richest and most diverse landscapes on Earth. Shri Singh said that nearly 60 per cent of the world’s wild Asian elephants live in India, making them a living symbol of the country’s ecological heritage. The Minister further stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s elephant reserves stand as a testament to the country’s commitment towards conservation.

India is home to one of the richest and most diverse landscapes on Earth. On #WorldElephantDay we can proudly say that nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephants live here, a living symbol of our ecological heritage. They embody majestic beauty, hold deep religious and… pic.twitter.com/Wns3CR9YlE

— Kirti Vardhan Singh (@KVSinghMPGonda) August 12, 2026

Shri Kriti Vardhan Singh also highlighted the role of elephants as ecosystem engineers. Shri Singh said that as elephants roam, they disperse seeds across long distances, giving rise to new plants, and that every step of an elephant helps keep nature in balance. He called upon everyone to unite to protect and preserve these gentle giants.

headline: Parliament Question: IGB Meeting Of BRICS Network University
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: IGB Meeting Of BRICS Network University

12 AUG 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

During India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, the Ministry of Education organized the BRICS Network University (BRICS NU) conference, virtually, on 20th July 2026. The theme of the meeting was "Need and Challenges of Preservation of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems in the Digital Age". The Conference was divided into three sessions - (i) Mapping, Identification and Systematic Documentation of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems across BRICS Countries, (ii) Preservation and Protection of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems and (iii) Role of Digital Technologies in Preserving Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems.

During these sessions, subject experts from India and BRICS member countries held deliberations on mapping, identification, systematic documentation, preservation, protection and using digital technologies in preserving traditional and indigenous knowledge systems. India shared the “Guiding Principles on Strengthening Collaboration on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge System” with the member countries of BRICS.

The International Governing Board Meeting (IGB) of the BRICS NU took place, virtually, on 21st July 2026. During the meeting, members of the IGB presented updates on the collaborative activities among the 178 participating universities across 11 International Thematic Groups (ITGs) in the BRICS NU.

Under the BRICS NU, each BRICS Member Country has the option to nominate two Higher Educational Institutes which work on subjects of focus in 11 International Thematic Groups (ITGs). India has 22 Institutions within the BRICS NU. India proposed “Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge System” as the 12th ITG during the BRICS NU and IGB meetings and has also been mentioned in the Declaration adopted during the 13th BRICS Education Ministers Meeting on 7th August 2026.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

(Release ID: 2298515)

headline: Parliament Question: Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme 2026

12 AUG 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has framed and approved the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to transform the education landscape into a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and learner-centric ecosystem. The Policy aims to enhance equity, quality and access to education for all, while promoting research and innovation as key components of higher education.

In pursuance with the vision of NEP 2020, the Ministry of Education has launched the Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme to attract and engage distinguished Indian-origin researchers, scientists and professionals with international research experience, to strengthen India's higher education and research ecosystem through research, mentorship and institutional capacity-building across national priority thematic areas. The Scheme provides for fellowships under three categories, namely Research Chair, Senior Fellow and Young Research Fellow.

Under the Scheme, seven institutions have been identified as Lead Institutions. As on date, more than 3,600 applications for fellowship and more than 400 applications from host institutions have been received.

The government has made provision of Rs 200 crore for the PMRC Scheme for the year 2026-27. The Scheme envisages India’s position as a global hub of research, innovation and knowledge creation by providing benefits of structured engagement of Indian-origin researchers and scientists to Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), national laboratories, and research centres. Details of scheme, eligibility criteria for fellows and host institutions are available at https://pmrc.education.gov.in/

headline: Parliament Question: Regulation and Oversight of Private Coaching Institution
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: Regulation and Oversight of Private Coaching Institution

12 AUG 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi

Keeping in view the growth in number of unregulated private coaching centres; instances of such centers charging exorbitant fees from students; loss of precious lives due to fire and other accidents; significance of mental well-being; and many malpractices being adopted by these centres, Ministry has circulated Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Center to States/UTs on 16.01.2024 for taking further action by way of appropriate legal framework. The guidelines for regulation of coaching centres are accessible at https://www.dohe-education.gov.in/documents/acts-and-policies/guidelines-for-regulation-of-coaching-center-ADNyEDOtQWa?pageTitle=Guidelines-for-Regulation-of-Coaching-Center

The Guidelines encompass several key aspects, including specifying conditions and necessary documents for registration, issues related to fees, outlining infrastructure prerequisites for establishing coaching centers, establishing a code of conduct for coaching centers; lay emphasis on significance of mental well-being, no batch segregation, maintenance of records, grievance/complaint redressal mechanism etc. The guidelines inter-alia provides for a coaching center to have a website with updated details of the qualification of tutors, details and duration of courses/curriculum, the fees being charged, easy exit policy, fee refund policy, number of students undertaking coaching from the center and number of students who finally succeeded in getting admission in Higher Education Institutions etc.

Education is a subject of the Concurrent List and both Central and State governments work collaboratively to provide equitable access to education. After issue of Guidelines by the Central Government, a number of States/UTs have brought out guidelines / regulations / legislations to regulate Private Coaching and tuition classes in their respective states/UTs, such as Andhra Pradesh Coaching Institutions (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2026, the Himachal Pradesh Private Coaching Centres (Registration and Regulation) Rules 2026, Policy and Guidelines for Registration, Control & Regulation of Coaching Institutes in the Union Territory of Puducherry, 2026, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Tamil Nadu Coaching Centres, 2026, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centers in Andaman and Nicobar Islands 2026, the Rajasthan Coaching Centres (Control and Regulation) Act, 2025, Jharkhand Coaching Centre (Control and Regulation), Act 2025, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centers in Tripura, 2025, the Assam Coaching Institutes (Control and Regulation) Act, 2025, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centres in the State of Nagaland, 2025, Haryana Registration and Regulation of Private Coaching Institutes Act, 2024.

Under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has also issued comprehensive guidelines on 13.11.2024 to address the issue of misleading advertisements in the coaching sector. These guidelines prohibit coaching centres from making false or misleading claims/advertisements to promote their services and from engaging in deceptive or unfair practices. It also provides that any person who is engaged in coaching shall not use names, photographs, testimonials or videos of successful candidates in an advertisement without the candidate's written consent. The guidelines also regulate unfair contracts and impose strict penalties under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, ensuring accountability and ethical practices in the coaching sector. CCPA imposes penalties on coaching institutes and directs them to discontinue the misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

headline: Parliament Question: Conduct of CBSE Sports Competitions and Technical Assistance
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: Conduct of CBSE Sports Competitions and Technical Assistance

12 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

CBSE Games are governed by the comprehensive CBSE Games (Guidelines) (available on the CBSE sports portal) and the annual circulars (e.g., Circular No. Acad 19/2026). Key provisions include:

Structure: Events are held at Cluster level (broadly state-based; higher-participation games such as Athletics, Basketball, Football (Boys), Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Table Tennis, Volleyball), Zonal level (for lower-participation games such as Archery, Badminton, Boxing, Chess, Football (Girls), Handball, Hockey, Judo, Shooting, Skating, Swimming, Taekwondo, Tennis, Yogasana), and National level. Certain games (Aerobics, Gymnastics, and Rope Skipping) are held directly at National level.

Age criteria: Calculated as on 31 December of the year of the event (e.g., for 2026- 27: Under-11 born on/after 01.01.2016; Under-14 on/after 01.01.2013; Under-17 on/after 01.01.2010; Under-19 on/after 01.01.2008).

Eligibility and participation: Online registration of students (UID-based), application to participate, and confirmation to the organising school. The winners of Cluster/Zonal level competitions qualify for Nationals. Foreign schools compete under Foreign Zone(s) and qualify directly to Nationals.

Organising schools: Selected via online applications, Regional Sports Committee recommendations, and finalisation by the National Sports Committee. Schools must have adequate infrastructure (preferably as per SAI specifications) and upload supporting videos.

Other rules: Cover eligibility documents, disqualification, safety measures, accommodation/meals (participants typically pay a prescribed daily charge), certificates (online generation); medals provided by CBSE, and sport-specific rules (generally aligned with recognised federations/SGFI where applicable). In case of clash/ambiguity, the latest circular prevails.

As per the CBSE Games (Guidelines), the organising school is responsible for hiring technically qualified and experienced umpires/referees/game officials from the District/State Sports Associations/Federations of the concerned game to ensure fair play.

CBSE provides a fixed Sports Grant to organising schools (not a variable year-wise budgetary allocation published separately for this purpose). As per the current Guidelines and Circulars (consistent across recent years, including 2023–24, 2024–25 and 2025–26 provisions):

Cluster/Zonal level: Rs 2,00,000

National level: Rs 3,00,000

Athletics and Swimming: Rs 4,00,000 (Cluster/Zonal) and Rs 5,00,000 (National).

Year | Total Grant allotted to schools in र

2023-2024 | 6,32,00,000

2024-2025 | 12,13,00,000

2025-2026 | 9,00,00,000

The grant is to be utilised for the approved heads (payment to referees/ technical officials/ observers, ground maintenance, sports equipments, tentage, videography, miscellaneous, etc.).

Organising schools must submit expenditure details in the prescribed Proforma along with a Utilisation Certificate certifying that the grant has been fully utilised for the sanctioned purpose. The proforma includes a detailed Statement of Income & Expenditure (covering accommodation, equipment, first-aid, tentage, referees/officials, ceremonies, photography, TA/DA to Observer, transport, etc.). The organising schools are required to get the proforma and accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant before uploading on CBSE Integrated Payment System (IPS) portal.

CBSE gets these proformas and accounts audited by internal as well as external audit teams.

Fair conduct and adherence to rules: Technically qualified officials from the concerned District/State Sports Associations/Federations are hired by the organizing schools to ensure fair play.

Grievance/Protest mechanism: Any protest must be submitted in writing to the Organising Secretary within 30 minutes of the declaration of the result, accompanied by a fee of Rs 1,000. It is considered by the Jury of Appeal. Parties are heard. If the protest is upheld, the fee is refunded; otherwise, it is forfeited. The Jury’s decision is final and binding and is reported (with full facts) to the CBSE Sports Cell.

All stakeholders are directed to follow the Rules of Sports & Games, and CBSE Games (Guidelines) available on the CBSE sports portal. Queries may be addressed to the CBSE Sports Cell (e.g., via the contact details given in the circulars).

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

(Release ID: 2298509)

### OVERVIEW
The Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, outlined the conduct, structure, eligibility criteria, and financial provisions of the CBSE Games for the 2026‑27 academic year in a Rajya Sabha written reply.

- Organising schools must hire technically qualified and experienced umpires/referees from District/State Sports Associations/Federations.  
- Protests must be submitted in writing to the Organising Secretary within 30 minutes of the result, with a Rs 1,000 fee; the Jury of Appeal reviews the protest, refunds the fee if upheld, otherwise forfeits it; the decision is final, binding, and reported to the CBSE Sports Cell.  
- Stakeholders are directed to follow the Rules of Sports & Games and CBSE Games Guidelines; queries may be directed to the CBSE Sports Cell.

headline: Parliament Question: Foreign University Campuses and Overseas Campuses of Indian Institutions
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: Foreign University Campuses and Overseas Campuses of Indian Institutions

12 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued 16 Letters of Intent (LoIs) to Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) from Australia, Italy, United Kingdom and the United States of America. UGC has issued LoIs to six FHEIs in Karnataka, six in Maharashtra, three in Delhi NCR and one in Tamil Nadu. Out of the six LoIs in Maharashtra, four FHEIs (University of York, University of Bristol, University of Aberdeen and Illinois Institute of Technology) have been given Letter of Approval to start academic operations in Mumbai. University of Southampton and University of New South Wales have already established their campuses in Gurugram and Bengaluru respectively.

IIT Madras, IIT Delhi and IIM Ahmedabad have established their overseas campuses at Zanzibar in 2023, Abu Dhabi in 2024 and Dubai respectively in 2025. IIM Ahmedabad launched a one-year fulltime MBA programme in Dubai campus in September 2025, along with a General Management programme, for professionals across the Middle-East, Asia and Africa. The programme has 35 students. IIT Madras, opened its campus at Zanzibar in 2023 - 35 students have graduated with M Tech degrees in Data Science and AI and Ocean Structures so far. Over 100 students are in various BS programmes in Data Science and Chemical Process Engineering. IIT Delhi established its offshore campus in Abu Dhabi, UAE in 2024 with nine UG, PG and Doctoral courses. In the academic year 2025-26, the campus had 171 students.

Studying abroad is a matter of individual will and choice, which is contingent on a variety of factors, including affordability, access to finance, exposure to foreign societies and aptitude for particular branches of studies. As per information provided by the Bureau of Immigration (BoI), Ministry of Home Affairs, the number of Indians who disclosed their purpose of visit as STUDY/EDUCATION while going abroad from 2021 to 2025 is as below:

Year | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025

Number of Students | 445580 | 752100 | 894758 | 760060 | 619264

The Government of India, including under National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) has undertaken several initiatives to ensure availability of high-quality education in the higher education, including through infrastructure upgradation of public funded educational institutions, accreditation of new institutions and courses which meet the criteria under National Accreditation Board, promotion of research & innovation and augmenting digital initiatives for accessibility. These initiatives have contributed to a wider pool of institutions and also in increasing the quality of educational facilities in the country.

In addition, University Grants Commission (UGC) has taken several initiatives to enhance quality of education, including financial support to HEIs, including issuing regulations for Joint/Dual/Twinning degree programmes, guidelines for Internship/Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Program, establishment of Research and Development Cells in HEIs, promoting the concept of Professor of Practice, accessibility guidelines and standards for Higher Educational Institutions and Universities, initiation of UTSAH Portal (Undertaking Transformative Strategies and Actions in Higher Education) to track achievements of NEP 2020, issuing Curriculum and Guidelines on Life Skills (Jeevan Kaushal) 2.0, launching of Malaviya Mission Teachers Training Programme (MMTTP) for continuous capacity building of faculties.

As an overall result, 52 Indian Institutions are now in the QS World University Ranking (QS WUR) 2027 which is India’s highest ever representation, marking an increase from 11 Indian institutions in QS WUR 2015. India is ranked 38th position globally as per Global Innovation Index (2025). India is considered to be one of the largest startup ecosystems in the world (top 3) in scale, funding and unicorn count.

Further, to attract international students to India, the Ministry has launched the ‘Study in India’ scheme in 2018 with the aim of promoting India as a global study destination providing world-class education at affordable costs. An integral part of the programme is the Study in India (SII) portal, a one-stop destination for admission and visa applications for all incoming foreign students and acts as a gateway to the Indian higher education ecosystem.

There are 1,289 universities, 48,246 colleges and 15,221 stand-alone institutions in the country, of which 87 universities, 5,380 colleges and 2,426 stand-alone institutions are located in Maharashtra. Maharashtra is among the top seven states in the country in terms of student enrolment in higher education, with approximately 46.53 lakh students. Higher education ecosystem in Maharashtra has been significantly strengthened through digital integration, quality accreditation, online learning, institutional governance and financial support through initiatives such as Academic Bank of Credits (ABC), Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR), Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM), SAMARTH and PM Vidyalaxmi.

The Government has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phases of RUSA, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/underserved areas. In Maharashtra, under the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), a total of 144 projects, with an approved amount of Rs. 1,431.31 crore (central share: Rs. 863.37 crore), have been approved under various components of the Scheme.

headline: Parliament Question: Draft UGC Regulations, 2025
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Parliament Question: Draft UGC Regulations, 2025

12 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

Education is a subject in the Concurrent List and both the Parliament and the state legislatures have powers to legislate. As per Entry 66 List I of Schedule VII to the Constitution of India, the power to legislate for "Co-ordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education or research and scientific and technical institutions", vests in the Central Government. Section 26 (1) (e) of University Grants Commission (UGC) Act, 1956 empowers UGC to make Regulations regarding ‘defining the qualifications that should ordinarily be required of any person to be appointed to the teaching staff of the University, having regard to the branch of education in which he is expected to give instruction'. Section 26 (1) (g) of UGC Act, 1956 empowers UGC to make regulations 'regulating the maintenance of standards and the co-ordination of work or facilities in Universities’.

The Draft UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges, 2025 were placed on the UGC website on 6 January 2025. In addition, UGC sought feedback from the Principal Secretaries, Higher Education Departments of all States; Higher Education Councils of all States; Offices of the Chancellors of all State Universities; IITs, IIMs, IISERs, IISc; and other regulatory bodies.

The UGC has decided to continue consultations to obtain broader stakeholder inputs before finalizing the Regulations. This approach is intended to ensure that all diverse views expressed on the proposed provisions, including those relating to the appointment of Vice-Chancellors, are duly considered as an integral part of the process of finalizing the Regulations.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

(Release ID: 2298506)
summaryText:

The Ministry of Education announced that the UGC will continue consultations on the Draft UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Other Academic Staff, 2025, before finalizing them, incorporating diverse stakeholder feedback including on Vice‑Chancellor appointments.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Draft regulations were posted on the UGC website on 6 January 2025.  
- UGC solicited feedback from Principal Secretaries, Higher Education Departments of all States; State Higher Education Councils; Chancellor offices of all State Universities; IITs, IIMs, IISERs, IISc; and other regulatory bodies.

headline: Empowering Governance through Digital Infrastructure
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Empowering Governance through Digital Infrastructure

12 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

Building a Connected and Citizen-Centric India

India's governance has undergone a fundamental transformation through Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI). Public services that once depended on extensive paperwork and physical offices are now available through integrated digital platforms. Over the past 12 years, DPI has connected citizens, governments and institutions on an unprecedented scale. It has made governance faster, transparent and more responsive to citizens' needs.

Digital infrastructure has also emerged as a cornerstone of India's economic growth. Digital Economy now contributes about 12–14% of India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and is projected to account for 20% over the next decade. India is now the world’s fifth-largest digitalised economy and the fourth-highest ranked G20 economy, according to the State of India’s Digital Economy Report 2026. As India marks its 80th Independence Day, the continued expansion of digital governance is strengthening service delivery, enabling economic opportunities and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Key Milestones in India’s Digital Self-Reliance Landscape

Electronics Manufacturing: Driving India's Self-Reliance

Guided by the vision of Make in India, India has emerged as a global hub for electronics manufacturing. Flagship initiatives, including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0), have strengthened domestic manufacturing in India.

7-Fold Growth in Electronics Production: Electronics production increased from ₹1.9 lakh crore in 2014–15 to ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26.

11-Fold Rise in Electronics Exports: Electronics exports grew from ₹38,000 crore to ₹4.24 lakh crore during the same period.

Third-largest Export Sector: Electronic goods have now become India's third-largest export category, with exports reaching USD 47.96 billion in FY 2025-26.

Employment and Women Participation: Electronic manufacturing ecosystem supports nearly 25 lakh jobs, with women accounting for nearly 30% of the workforce.

Building India's Semiconductor Ecosystem

The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 with an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore to strengthen India's semiconductor ecosystem. Under ISM 1.0, 12 semiconductor units worth ₹1.64 lakh crore have been approved. Three facilities have already started commercial production, with another unit expected to commence operations this year.

Mobile Phones: A Major Driver of Growth

Global Mobile Manufacturing Hub: India is now the world's 2nd largest mobile phone manufacturer, with mobile phones rising from the 153rd largest export item in FY 2014-15 to become India's largest export product in FY 2025-26.

33-fold increase in mobile phone production: Production rose from ₹18,000 crore in 2014–15 to ₹6.27 lakh crore in 2025–26.

165-fold surge in mobile phone exports: Exports increased from ₹1,500 crore to ₹2.59 lakh crore over the same period.

Employment and Women Participation: Out of 12 lakh jobs in mobile manufacturing segment, women constitute nearly 70% of the workforce.

Enhanced Telecommunications Infrastructure

Telephone Connectivity: Telephone connections increased from 93.3 crore in 2014 to 134.8+ crore at the end of June 2026.

Higher Tele-density: Tele-density grew from 75.23% in 2014 to 94.31% at the end of June 2026.

Wireless Mobile Subscribers: The number of active wireless mobile subscribers reached 1201.06 million in June 2026.

Internet and Digital Connectivity

Internet Users Quadrupled: Internet subscribers increased from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 109.2+ crore at the end of March 2026.

Affordable Mobile Data: Wireless data cost dropped drastically from ₹308/GB in 2014 to ₹7.51/GB in 2026, making digital services more affordable.

Mobile broadband speed: Average mobile broadband download speed has increased from 13.67 Mbps in March 2022 to 132.00 Mbps in December 2025 as per Ookla’s global speedtest index.

Nationwide 5G Rollout: 5G services are now available in 99.9% of districts across all States and Union Territories. The number of 5G Base Transceiver Stations (BTSs) has now reached 5.63 lakh in June 2026.

Expanding Rural Mobile Connectivity: A total of 6.31 lakh villages have been now covered with 4G services by BSNL and other operators.

Connectivity under BharatNet Initiative: As of June 2026, 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats are service-ready, supported by over 8.5 lakh route km of optical fibre cable.

PM-WANI: PM-WANI provides affordable public Wi-Fi through a distributed network of public data offices and other ecosystem partners. Over 4 lakh hotspots have been deployed nationwide, as of 28 February 2026. New reforms introduced in May 2026 enable QR-based authentication, 15, 30 and 60-minute Wi-Fi plans, and standardised hotspot names.

India is Preparing for the 6G Era

The Bharat 6G Vision aims to position India among the global leaders in 6G technology by 2030, with a focus on indigenous research, intellectual property, standards development and next-generation telecom innovation.

UPI: Powering Seamless Digital Payments

UPI accounts for nearly 50% of global real-time payment transaction volume, making it the world's largest real-time payment system by volume.

Volume of Transactions: UPI processed 24,161.69 crore transactions worth ₹314.23 lakh crore in FY 2025–26.

India’s Largest Digital Payments Network: UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system.

Share of UPI in India's Digital Payments: UPI accounted for 85% of India's digital payment transactions by volume in FY 2025–26.

Monthly Transactions Soar: UPI transactions increased from 0.01 crore in a month in 2016 to 2,000+ crore transactions in a month by 2025, reflecting its rapid adoption across India.

UPI Goes Global: UPI is now accepted in 11 foreign countries like Cambodia, Singapore, UAE, France, Mauritius etc.

Digital Commerce

Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC): ONDC is building an open digital commerce ecosystem connecting buyers and sellers across platforms.

By June 2026, it had over 20 crore buyers, 5 lakh sellers, presence in 1,000 cities and nearly 90 lakh monthly transactions.

Its integration with eSaras and Indiahandmade has expanded market access for SHGs, weavers and artisans across 11+ buyer apps, while the Sahayak WhatsApp Bot supports small businesses in 5 languages.

Government e-Marketplace (GeM): GeM has transformed public procurement by making it transparent, efficient and paperless.

By June 2026, it recorded over ₹18.4 lakh crore in cumulative Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), including ₹5 lakh crore in FY 2025–26, and enabled over 11 lakh MSMEs to access government markets.

SWAYATT (Startup Runway for Women and Youth-led Enterprises) initiative, promotes inclusive public procurement through the GeM by enabling startups, women and youth-led enterprises to directly access government buyers.

By FY 2025–26, women-led businesses recorded ₹83,323 crore and startups ₹54,005.8 crore in cumulative order value, demonstrating the initiative’s growing reach.

E-Governance Initiatives Revolutionising G2C Services

DigiLocker: DigiLocker is replacing physical documents with a secure digital wallet. As of 31 July 2026, the platform has registered over 72 crore users and issued more than 934+ Cr documents.

UMANG: UMANG has become a single digital gateway for government services, expanding from 166 services in 2017 to 2585 services as of 23 July 2026. Transactions have grown from 4.6 crore to over 798 crore as of 23 July 2026, reflecting widespread digital adoption.

Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Aadhaar generation increased from 0.42 crore in 2010-11 to over 145 crore by July 2026.

Common Service Centres: CSCs provide physical access points for Government-to-Citizen (G2C) e-services, reducing the need to visit government offices. As of June 2026, more than 5.16 lakh CSCs were functional across India.

Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): Aadhaar-linked DBT enables direct transfer of welfare benefits from 318 schemes across 56 Ministries into beneficiaries’ bank accounts. More than ₹52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT across the country. Read More: The Digital India

Digital Platforms Driving Educational Access

DIKSHA: DIKSHA provides curriculum-linked content, QR-coded textbooks, teacher training and accessible learning resources. It has 2.35 crore registered users and 3.58 lakh daily active users, as on 10 August 2026.

SWAYAM: SWAYAM offers free courses from Class IX to postgraduate level. The platform hosts over 20,000 courses across disciplines with 6.5 crore+ total enrollments, as of 10 August 2026.

SWAYAM Prabha: It uses 40 DTH channels to broadcast high-quality educational programmes 24×7 through the GSAT-15 satellite, enabling students to access learning without internet connectivity.

PM e-Vidya: PM e-Vidya integrates DIKSHA, SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, community radio and educational television to support uninterrupted and inclusive learning.

Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR): APAAR provides students with a unique digital academic identity for storing and verifying academic records. More than 33.74 crore APAAR IDs had been generated by June 2026.

A Stronger Framework Against Exam Fraud

The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 31 July 2026, proposes tougher penalties and a time-bound justice mechanism. Under the Bill, individual offenders face 5–10 years’ imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh, service providers face fines up to ₹5 crore and an 8-year ban, while organised exam-fraud syndicates face 7–10 years’ imprisonment and a minimum fine of ₹10 crore. Investigations must be completed within 2 months, trials within 3 months of filing the chargesheet, and appeals before the High Court are to be disposed of within 3 months of admission.

Powering India’s Digital Workforce

FutureSkills PRIME: It equips learners with cutting-edge skills essential in today's rapidly evolving digital landscape. The platform has 34 lakh+ registered users for digital skills, as of 10 August 2026.

Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH): SIDH brings skilling, digital learning and employment opportunities onto a single platform. As of 2 August 2026, it has 20.10 million registrations, offers 3,643 self-paced courses, and has generated 1 million+ opportunities.

National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT): NIELIT delivers digital literacy and skill development programmes, including Awareness in Computer Concepts (ACC) and Course on Computer Concepts (CCC), through 56 centres and over 9,000 partner institutes across India. More than 31.92 lakh candidates have been trained over the last three financial years.

IndiaAI Mission: The IndiaAI Mission is strengthening AI education, infrastructure and responsible AI adoption. It is promoting AI skilling across schools, higher education institutions and professional training programmes through initiatives such as IndiaAI Kosh. Read More: Transforming India with AI

India’s Growing Digital Rise

India’s digital rise is transforming the way citizens, businesses and institutions interact with the government and economy. A rapidly expanding digital ecosystem is enabling faster services, greater transparency and wider access. Digital Public Infrastructure is creating a strong foundation for innovation, entrepreneurship and inclusive growth. The growing adoption of emerging technologies is opening new opportunities across sectors and strengthening India’s global digital presence. Digital capabilities are also making governance more responsive, efficient and citizen-centric. This transformation is positioning technology as a key enabler of economic opportunity and social development. Together, these advances are strengthening the foundations of a digitally empowered and Viksit Bharat.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
India’s Digital Public Infrastructure has experienced rapid expansion, marked by record growth in electronics manufacturing, semiconductor investment, telecom connectivity, and digital payments, positioning the country as a globally integrated, citizen‑centric digital economy.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Electronics production grew 7‑fold from ₹1.9 lakh crore (2014‑15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025‑26).  
- Electronics exports rose 11‑fold from ₹38,000 crore to ₹4.24 lakh crore; sector is now India’s third‑largest export at USD 47.96 billion (FY 2025‑26).  
- “Semicon 2.0” approved with an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore; 12 semiconductor units approved under ISM 1.0 totalling ₹1.64 lakh crore; three facilities in commercial production, another to start this year.  
- Mobile phone production increased 33‑fold from ₹18,000 crore (2014‑15) to ₹6.27 lakh crore (2025‑26); exports grew 165‑fold from ₹1,500 crore to ₹2.59 lakh crore; mobile phones are now India’s largest export product, supporting ~12 lakh jobs with women comprising ~70 % of the workforce.  
- Telephone connections rose from 93.3 crore (2014) to 134.8 crore (June 2026); tele‑density grew from 75.23 % to 94.31 % (June 2026).  
- Wireless mobile subscribers reached 1,201.06 million (June 2026).  
- Internet users grew from 25.15 crore (2014) to 109.2 crore (March 2026).  
- Wireless data cost fell from ₹308/GB (2014) to ₹7.51/GB (2026); average mobile broadband speed increased from 13.67 Mbps (Mar 2022) to 132.00 Mbps (Dec 2025).  
- 5G services available in 99.9 % of districts; 5.63 lakh 5G BTSs (June 2026); 6.31 lakh villages covered with 4G by BSNL and others.  
- BharatNet: 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats service‑ready; >8.5 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid.  
- PM‑WANI: 4 lakh Wi‑Fi hotspots deployed (as of 28 Feb 2026); May 2026 reforms introduce QR authentication, 15/30/60‑minute Wi‑Fi plans, and standardised hotspot names.  
- Bharat 6G Vision aims to position India as a global leader in 6G by 2030, emphasizing indigenous research, IP, standards development, and next‑generation telecom innovation.  
- UPI processed 24,161.69 crore transactions worth ₹314.23 lakh crore in FY 2025‑26; serves 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks; UPI accounts for 85 % of India’s digital payment volume by transactions; monthly transactions rose from 0.01 crore (2016) to 2,000+ crore (2025); UPI is now accepted in 11 foreign countries.  
- Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) had >20 crore buyers, 5 lakh sellers, presence in 1,000 cities, and ~90 lakh monthly transactions by June 2026; integrated with eSaras and Indiahandmade; Sahayak WhatsApp Bot supports small businesses in 5 languages.  
- Government e‑Marketplace (GeM) recorded cumulative GMV >₹18.4 lakh crore; FY 2025‑26 GMV ₹5 lakh crore; enabled >11 lakh MSMEs to access government markets.  
- SWAYATT initiative reported women‑led businesses achieving ₹83,323 crore (FY 2025‑26).

headline: Ministry of Textiles to Celebrate Women Weavers Through ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

Ministry of Textiles to Celebrate Women Weavers Through ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’

Over 100 Women Weavers from Six Handloom Clusters to share their stories of Resilience, Creativity and Role in preserving India’s Weaving Traditions

12 AUG 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, will organise ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’, a special gathering celebrating the women behind India’s handlooms and recognising their inspiring journeys, voices and contributions to the weaving heritage of the country. The programme will be held on 13 August 2026, at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi.

The event will bring together 100+ women weavers from six handloom clusters across India, providing a platform to celebrate their lived experiences, resilience, creativity and role in carrying forward India’s rich weaving traditions.

The programme will also witness the release of an anthology featuring the inspiring stories, journeys and voices of these women weavers, bringing their experiences from the loom to a wider audience and highlighting the human stories that lie at the heart of India’s handloom sector.

The event will be graced by Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Textiles and Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms). Ms. Kanta Singh, Deputy Country Representative, UN Women India, will be the Guest of Honour.

‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’ seeks to place women weavers at the centre of the conversation on India’s handloom heritage, acknowledging not only their contribution to the sector but also their individual journeys, aspirations and voices.

headline: Union Minister of Textiles inaugurates IIHT SUTRA 2026, the first National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

Union Minister of Textiles inaugurates IIHT SUTRA 2026, the first National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology

Three landmark MoUs signed to strengthen industry, research and academic partnerships for transforming handloom education

12 AUG 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, today organised IIHT SUTRA 2026 – The Inaugural National Conclave of the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.

Conceived as a first-of-its-kind national platform, IIHT SUTRA 2026 brought together policymakers, academia, industry leaders, research institutions, distinguished alumni and students to deliberate on the future of handloom education and its role in strengthening India's handloom ecosystem.

Organised under the theme "IIHTs: Weaving the Future of the Indian Handloom Sector – Educate. Innovate. Transform.", the conclave marked a significant step towards repositioning the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology (IIHTs) as centres of excellence for technical education, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and industry collaboration.

The conclave was inaugurated by Shri Giriraj Singh, Union Minister of Textiles, in the presence of Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Textiles, Dr. Beena M., Development Commissioner (Handlooms) and other distinguished dignitaries representing Government, industry, academia and the handloom sector.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Textiles Shri. Giriraj Singh, emphasised that India's handloom sector is one of the finest expressions of the country's cultural heritage while also serving as an important source of livelihoods, women's empowerment, exports and sustainable economic development. He observed that preserving India's handloom traditions must go hand in hand with technological advancement, innovation, entrepreneurship and research. He underscored the important role of the IIHTs in developing skilled technocrats capable of supporting productivity enhancement, design innovation, technology upgradation and the long-term competitiveness of the handloom sector.

The Minister highlighted that the six Central IIHTs and five State IIHTs have, over the past seven decades, produced generations of skilled professionals who today contribute significantly to industry, entrepreneurship, exports, research and public institutions. He also noted the recent expansion of B.Tech programmes, strengthening of research initiatives, modernisation of laboratories and infrastructure, student support measures and international training programmes undertaken by the IIHTs.

In her address, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, emphasised the need to continuously modernise handloom education by aligning curricula with emerging technologies, strengthening industry partnerships, promoting applied research and encouraging innovation-led learning. She observed that IIHTs must evolve as institutions capable of preparing graduates not only for employment but also for entrepreneurship, leadership and research in the textile and handloom sectors.

Welcoming the participants, Dr. Beena M., IAS, Development Commissioner (Handlooms) described IIHT SUTRA as a long-term institutional initiative of the Ministry of Textiles aimed at creating a collaborative national platform for the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology. She stated that the initiative seeks to strengthen partnerships among Government, industry, academia, research institutions and alumni while enabling IIHTs to emerge as future-ready institutions supporting innovation, sustainability, entrepreneurship and technological advancement in the handloom sector.

A major highlight of the inaugural session was the exchange of three strategic Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) designed to strengthen institutional collaboration across complementary domains:

Grasim Industries Limited – Industry Partnership for curriculum enrichment, internships, industry exposure, skill development and collaborative initiatives.

Northern India Textile Research Association (NITRA) – Research and Technology Partnership for collaborative research, testing, innovation, technical support and capacity building.

Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Sambalpur – Academic and Management Partnership for leadership development, entrepreneurship, innovation, faculty development and institutional capacity building.

These partnerships are expected to provide a structured framework for closer engagement between IIHTs and leading institutions from industry, research and management education, thereby enhancing the quality and relevance of technical education in the handloom sector.

During the programme, meritorious students from the IIHTs were honoured with Gold Medals and Rank Certificates in recognition of their outstanding academic performance. The Ministry also released "Handloom Change Makers", a publication celebrating the achievements of distinguished IIHT alumni who have made notable contributions across industry, entrepreneurship, exports, research and public service.

The Union Minister also launched the Ministry's film on IIHTs titled "Weaving India's Handloom Future", presenting the journey, achievements and future vision of the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology. The film highlights the contribution of IIHTs in developing skilled professionals and supporting the transformation of India's handloom sector.

The conclave also featured an exhibition showcasing student innovations, institutional achievements, live demonstrations, research initiatives and emerging technologies adopted by the IIHTs. Participants had the opportunity to interact with students, faculty members and alumni while experiencing the technological and educational capabilities of the institutes.

The post-lunch technical session included a panel discussion on "Strengthening Handloom Education through Industry–Academia Collaboration: Curriculum, Skills and Future Readiness." Eminent representatives from industry, academia, research institutions and distinguished alumni deliberated on curriculum reforms, industry partnerships, applied research, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, skill development and institutional collaboration required to prepare the next generation of professionals for the evolving textile and handloom sector.

IIHT SUTRA 2026 represents a significant step towards strengthening the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology through strategic partnerships, innovation, research and academic excellence, while preparing future-ready professionals for the evolving needs of the Indian handloom sector.

headline: From Financial Constraints to Educational Confidence: How Scholarship Support Helped Bhaskar Saini Continue His B.Tech. Education
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Constraints to Educational Confidence: How Scholarship Support Helped Bhaskar Saini Continue His B.Tech. Education

12 AUG 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Access to quality education can play an important role in helping students pursue their aspirations and build better opportunities for the future. However, for students from families with limited incomes, financial difficulties can become a major challenge in meeting college expenses and continuing higher education.

Demonstrating how scholarship assistance can provide relief to students facing economic challenges, Mr Bhaskar Saini, a 19-year-old student belonging to the Other Backward Class (OBC) category, is pursuing B.Tech. education in Mechanical Engineering. Coming from a middle-class family, he faced difficulties in managing the expenses related to education, including books, hostel and other academic requirements. Despite these challenges, Bhaskar remained focused on his studies and skill development, with the aspiration of securing a good job and improving his family's financial condition through higher education and technical knowledge.

In 2025-26, educational financial assistance of ₹1,15,400 was provided to Bhaskar. The support helped reduce the financial burden on his family and enabled him to continue his engineering education without interruption. It also allowed him to focus more on his academics and career preparation.

With the financial burden related to his education reduced, Bhaskar has been able to continue his B.Tech. studies with greater confidence. He is currently pursuing Mechanical Engineering and improving his technical skills to prepare himself for future employment opportunities.

Talking about the support generated by the scholarship, Bhaskar Saini said,

“I received financial assistance for my educational expenses, which reduced the financial burden on my family. This support helped me continue my studies without interruption and focus more on academics and career preparation. Currently, I am successfully pursuing my engineering studies and improving my technical skills for future employment opportunities.”

Bhaskar's story highlights how timely educational financial assistance can provide meaningful support to students facing financial constraints. By reducing the pressure of educational expenses, the support has enabled him to continue his higher education and work towards his aspiration of securing a good job, strengthening his family's financial stability and building a better future.

headline: Empowering Girls Through Safe and Affordable Accommodation: How PM-AJAY is Supporting Access to Higher Education in Manipur
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Empowering Girls Through Safe and Affordable Accommodation: How PM-AJAY is Supporting Access to Higher Education in Manipur

100-bedded SC Girls Hostel constructed at Dhanamanjuri University, Imphal West, MANIPUR at a cost Rs 3.50 Crores

12 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

For students from remote and rural areas, access to safe and affordable accommodation can play an important role in enabling them to pursue higher education.

Recognising this need, a 100-bedded SC Girls Hostel was constructed at Dhanamanjuri University, Imphal West, MANIPUR under the Hostel Component of the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY). The facility is being used by students from different communities, with SC students from far-flung areas of Manipur among the beneficiaries.

Constructed during 2022-23 at a cost of Rs 3.50 Crores under PM-AJAY, the hostel has significantly improved access to higher education for girl students from remote and rural parts of the State. Dhanamanjuri University is one of the reputed institutions in Manipur and attracts students from all districts, making accessible residential facilities an important support for students pursuing higher education.

100-Bedded SC Girls Hostel at Dhanamanjuri University, Imphal West

The hostel provides safe and affordable accommodation, enabling students to pursue higher education without the difficulties associated with daily travel or private lodging. The facility has become an important support system for girls seeking better educational opportunities and academic growth, particularly those travelling from distant parts of Manipur.

Hostel facility supporting higher education for girls from remote areas

The impact of the intervention is reflected in its utilisation. As of 29 May 2026, 76 students were residing in the hostel. By providing residential support close to the university, the facility is helping students overcome accommodation and commuting-related challenges and continue their academic pursuits in a secure and supportive environment.

Safe Accommodation | Affordable Stay | Better Access to Higher Education

The 100-bedded SC Girls Hostel at Dhanamanjuri University demonstrates how targeted educational infrastructure under PM-AJAY can strengthen access to higher education for students from far-flung areas. By providing safe and affordable accommodation, the initiative is supporting girls in pursuing higher education and creating a stronger foundation for their academic growth.

headline: The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors

“Driving Growth, Resilience and Food Security”

12 AUG 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi

Driving Agricultural Transformation

India’s agriculture and allied sectors are witnessing a significant transformation, marked by rising productivity, stronger farmer support systems, and greater resilience. Agriculture remains the backbone of India's economy, providing livelihoods to approximately 46.1 percent of the workforce. Livestock and fisheries have maintained stable growth of 5-6 percent, strengthening rural incomes and supporting agricultural diversification. Over the past decade, sustained policy interventions have improved access to credit, insurance, and markets, and accelerated the adoption of digital technologies. Growing investments in food processing, cooperatives, livestock, dairy, and fisheries are enabling greater value addition, income diversification, and employment across the agricultural value chain.

Strengthening the Agricultural Economy

The GVA of the Agriculture and Allied Sector increased from Rs.20.94 lakh crore in 2014-15 to an estimated Rs.52.08 lakh crore in 2025-26.

Budget allocation for the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare increased from Rs.27,663 crore in 2013-14 to Rs.1,40,528.78 crore in 2026-27.

Harvesting Higher Production

Total foodgrain production increased from 265.05 million tonnes in 2013-14 to 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26 (Third Advance Estimates).

Horticulture production increased from 280.70 million tonnes in 2013-14 to approximately 377.78 million tonnes in 2025-26 (Second Advance Estimates).

Oilseeds production increased from 27.51 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 43.06 million tonnes in 2025-26 (Third Advance Estimates).

Securing Farmers' Livelihoods

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)

More than Rs.4.47 lakh crore has been transferred directly into farmers’ bank accounts through 23 instalments under the Scheme.

Under the 23rd instalment, more than 9.49 crore farmers benefited, with over Rs.18,984 crore released.

The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)

Since its launch in 2016-17, over 92.46 crore farmer applications have been insured.

Claims worth Rs.1.96 lakh crore have been disbursed up to December 2025, benefiting around 24.31 crore farmers.

Minimum Support Prices (MSP)

Total procurement increased from 698.7 million tonnes during 2004-2014 to 1,229.2 million tonnes during 2014-2026.

Total MSP value increased from Rs.7.41 lakh crore during 2004-2014 to Rs.26.32 lakh crore during 2014-2026 (up to February 2026).

MSP for Paddy (Grade A) increased from Rs.1,400 per quintal in 2014-15 to Rs.2,461 per quintal in 2026-27.

MSP for Wheat increased from Rs.1,400 per quintal in 2014-15 to Rs.2,585 per quintal in 2026-27.

The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme

As on 3rd August 2026,

7.28 crore Kisan Credit Card (KCC) accounts were operational across the country in 2025-26.

The amount outstanding under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme stood at Rs.10.08 lakh crore.

The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PMKMY)

As of February 2026, around 24.96 lakh farmers have been enrolled under the scheme.

Towards Sustainable Agriculture

The Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme

26.09 crore soil health cards have been issued as of July 2026.

⁠In addition, over 70,002 Krishi Sakhis have been trained to provide soil health advisories and support informed farm practices.

Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)

Since its inception (as of June 2026), 18.93 lakh hectares of area have been covered, benefiting 33.63 lakh farmers.

Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER)

Since its inception (as on 30 June 2026), 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming benefitting 2.74 lakh farmers.

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)

During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission.

33.89 lakh farmers have been made aware of natural farming.

More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM)

As on 2nd August 2026,

Nearly 11.49 lakh off-grid solar pumps have been installed for agricultural use.

More than 15.89 lakh agricultural pumps are covered through feeder-level solarisation.

Around 1,726 MW of decentralized solar power capacity was commissioned on farmers’ land.

Over 21.77 lakh farmers benefited across the country.

Ensuring Food for All

As of February 2026, under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), against the intended coverage of 81.35 crore, the States/UTs have identified 80.56 crore persons for the provision of subsidized foodgrains.

Around 79.8 crore beneficiaries are covered across the country under NFSA, as of December 2025.

Centre to spend Rs. 25,530 crore in next 5 years under SARTHAK PDS - Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling-Income with Automation in PDS.

The Scheme will work towards fulfilling India's commitment to 81.35 crore persons covered under NFSA.

Building Stronger Rural Institutions through Cooperatives and FPOs

10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been registered across the country as of July 2026.

79,630 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) have been sanctioned for computerization across 31 States and Union Territories.

63,707 PACS have been onboarded on the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) based national software as of 05th August 2026.

Connecting Farms to Markets

National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)

As of June 2026, 1,656 mandis have been integrated.

1.89 crore farmers and 2.78 lakh traders have been registered on e-NAM.

Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI)

As of July 2026, 12,353 storage infrastructure projects with a storage capacity of 369.18 LMT have been sanctioned in the last ten years.

Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)

Interest subvention support has been extended to 18,893 warehouses, 3,110 cold stores/cold chain projects and 2,105 integrated primary and secondary processing units.

Food Processing Reforms

Enhanced Financial Support for Food Processing

Budget allocation for the Ministry of Food Processing Industries increased from Rs.785.86 crore in 2014-15 to Rs.4,064 crore in 2026-27.

Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)

Incentives amounting to Rs.3,271.44 crore have been disbursed up to June 2026.

The investments undertaken under the Scheme have resulted in the creation of food processing capacity of 34 lakh metric tonnes per annum.

Sales of PLI-supported products increased from Rs.58,758 crore in FY 2019-20 to Rs.1,08,854 crore in FY 2025-26.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY)

As of June 2026, 1,256 projects (post-harvest infrastructure and processing facilities) have been completed or are operational, benefitting about 37.76 lakh farmers.

294.21 LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity created, generating 9.16 lakh employment opportunities across the country.

Taking Indian Agriculture Global

The value of agricultural exports increased from USD 32.08 billion in 2014-15 to USD 54.70 billion in 2025-26, recording a growth of about 70.5 percent.

Share of processed food exports increased from 13.7 percent in 2014-15 to 20.4 percent in 2024-25, a nearly 49 percent rise.

Technology at the Farmgate

Under the Digital Agriculture Mission

As on 3rd August 2026

More than 10.31 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across the country. Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country.

AI-Enabled Initiatives:

National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS)- As of July 2026, this tool is being used by over 10,000 extension workers supporting 73 crops over 436 pests.

BharatVistaar- As of July 2026, the platform has served over 3 lakh farmers and addressed more than 72 lakh farmer queries.

Empowering Farmers Through Knowledge

Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs)

As of June 2026,

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has established 731 KVKs across the country.

Around 58.02 lakh farmers were trained between 2021-22 and 2023-24.

An additional 18.56 lakh farmers were trained during the first ten months of 2024-25.

Agricultural Diversification and the Growth of Allied Sectors

Livestock and Dairy as Drivers of Rural Economic Growth

The livestock sector has recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.77 percent since 2014-15. In the Union Budget 2026-27, Rs.6,153.46 crore has been allocated to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

Indigenous and non-descript cattle productivity reached 1,343.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 927 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15.

Buffalo productivity reached 2,365.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1880 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15.

Average bovine milk productivity has reached 2,251 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1,648 kg per animal per year in 2014-15.

India holds the leading global position in milk production, accounting for nearly 25 percent of global output.

Per capita milk availability reached 485 grams per day in 2024-25, compared to the global average of 394 grams per day.

Milk production has increased by 70 percent, rising from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 248 million tonnes in 2024-25.

Poultry and meat production have also expanded, with India ranking second in egg production and fourth in meat production globally:

Egg production has grown by 90 percent, increasing from 78.48 billion eggs in 2014-15 to 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25.

Per capita egg availability has risen from 62 eggs per annum in 2014-15 to 106 eggs per annum in 2024-25.

Meat Production has increased from 6.69 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 10.50 million tonnes in 2024-25.

Strengthening Fisheries Infrastructure, Market Access and Credit Support

The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record Rs.2,761.80 crore to fisheries under the Blue Revolution initiatives.

Fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, up from 95.79 lakh tonnes in FY 2013-14.

Seafood exports increased from USD 3.64 billion in 2013-14 to around USD 8.46 billion in 2025-26.

Fisheries Infrastructure and Market Access

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)

Rs.2,500 crore allocated under the Union Budget 2026-27.

As on April 2026, Key activities approved:

28,489 fish transportation and handling units

1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, and 117 fish retail markets

775 cold storages and ice plants, and 24 wholesale fish markets

Institutional Credit Support for fisheries

6.83 lakh applications were received under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC), of which 6.77 lakh were accepted. Of which, 4.82 lakh applications were sanctioned, indicating a meaningful conversion of demand into credit access as of early 2026.

KCC benefits have reached 4.39 lakh fishers. Insurance coverage has been provided to 33 lakh beneficiaries. An average of 7.44 lakh fisher families received livelihood assistance during lean fishing periods.

Strengthening Livestock through Infrastructure and Entrepreneurship

National Livestock Mission

As on 4th August 2026,

4,084 breed multiplication farms for poultry, sheep, goat, pig, camel, horse, and donkey have been approved.

1.61 lakh metric tonnes of quality fodder seed have been produced.

Entrepreneurship Development Programme under the National Livestock Mission, as on 11th August 2026,

4,321 projects approved, worth Rs.2,948.68 crore total project cost with the Rs.1,386.18 crore approved subsidy

Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)

Projects approved with 418 lakh litres/day of milk processing capacity and value-addition capacity as on 4th August 2026.

Bharat Pashudhan

As of 6th August 2026,

Livestock Owners Registered: 9.84 crore, Pashu Aadhaar Issued: Over 38.53 crore, All Vaccinations: 168.67 crore.

National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD)

As on June 2026,

36,611 new Dairy Cooperative Societies have been organised.

34,557 village-level dairy cooperative societies have been strengthened.

168 lakh litres/day of milk chilling capacity has been created.

76,748 milk quality testing devices have been distributed.

Advancing Livestock Breeding, Productivity, and Animal Health

A total of 47,687 Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRIs) have been trained, 24 IVF laboratories established, 48 semen stations sanctioned, and 28 heifer rearing centres approved under RGM as on 4th August 2026.

During the last five years, over 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been carried out under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme, benefiting nearly 5.98 crore farmers.

Accelerated Breed Improvement programme: As on 4th August 2026, 7,959 embryos transferred, 1,666 pregnancies established, and 1,223 calves born. Out of which 1,142 of the calves are females.

Strengthening Animal Health and Risk Mitigation

Livestock productivity and income stability are closely linked to disease control. Under

National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP)

As of March 2026, 132.49 crore doses of the Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccine have been administered.

Brucellosis Control Programme: As of March 2026, 3.17 crores, 4-8 months old bovine female calf for Brucellosis have been vaccinated in the country since inception. 296.74 lakh vaccine doses administered to eligible female calves to prevent brucellosis and strengthen livestock health during the last five years alone.

Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs)

4,019 MVUs are operational across 29 States/UTs, delivering doorstep veterinary services through the toll-free number 1962 as of July 2026.

Benefited 119.77 lakh farmers and treated 245.05 lakh animals, significantly boosting farmer confidence and supporting the livestock sector as a viable enterprise.

headline: Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
fullText:
Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi

Hindi Plays an Important Role in Strengthening Good Governance and Taking Ayush to the People: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Emphasis on Strengthening Use of Hindi and Public Outreach in Ministry of Ayush

12 AUG 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

The third meeting of the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Ayush was held today at Kartavya Bhawan-I, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

The meeting was attended by Hon’ble Members of Parliament Shri Rahul Singh Lodhi and Shri Gyaneshwar Patil, along with Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, members of the Committee and senior officials of the Ministry and its subordinate institutions.

Addressing the meeting, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the Hindi Advisory Committee is not merely a formal body but an important platform for strengthening the use and promotion of Hindi in the Ministry and making it an effective medium for public welfare and communication.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the country is moving forward with the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has laid special emphasis on the preservation, promotion and wider use of Indian languages. Shri Jadhav noted that the Prime Minister’s consistent use of Hindi at national and international forums has enhanced the recognition and respect for Hindi globally.

Shri Jadhav said that he makes efforts to ensure that maximum official work in his office is undertaken in Hindi. He urged officers and employees not to view the use of Hindi merely as a formal or constitutional obligation, but to make it an effective instrument of good governance, transparency and public outreach and an integral part of their day-to-day work.

Highlighting the importance of Indian languages in the Ayush sector, Shri Jadhav said that Ayush represents India’s rich and ancient knowledge tradition. Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy are gaining increasing popularity not only in India but also across the world.

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, highlighted the efforts being made by the Ministry to promote the use of Hindi in official work, correspondence, publications, website, social media and public relations activities. He also informed the Committee about initiatives to encourage officers and employees to use Hindi through training programmes, workshops and incentive schemes.

The Committee discussed the need to make Ayush-related knowledge, research, scientific literature, public welfare schemes and achievements of the Ministry widely available in Hindi and other Indian languages. The members also deliberated on making Ayush-related information more accessible through Indian languages and further strengthening its outreach among the general public.

The Ministry’s Hindi house journal ‘Apratim Ayush’ was also released during the meeting. Smt. Purnima Bose, Deputy Director, Department of Official Language, Ministry of Ayush, welcomed the participants, while Dr. Prakash Kumar, Assistant Director, Ministry of Ayush, conducted the proceedings.

The meeting was also attended by non-official members Markandey Rai, Thinles Dorje, Sunil Mehru, Ramya Krishna Kanaparthi and Hemchandra Vaidya.

(Release ID: 2298425)

headline: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
fullText:
Ministry of Cooperation

BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT

12 AUG 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

The implementation of Bharat Taxi Services is being carried out in a phased manner across the country. The implementation includes registration and onboarding of Sarathis (drivers), customer enrolment, training programmes and expansion of services to identified cities and States. As on 04.08.2026, the platform has registered 8.48 lakh Sarathis (drivers) and 44.27 lakh customers. The platform is facilitating 11,106 daily rides and has enabled cumulative earnings of ₹83.70 crore for Sarathis.

The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), in other cities and States is subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders.

The details of operation of Bharat Taxi in various cities and average daily rides, as on 04.08.2026, are as under:

City | Average Daily rides

Delhi- NCR | 5574

Chandigarh | 190

Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi are separate mobility platforms operating under different institutional frameworks. Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-based mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, whereas Yatri Sathi is a mobility platform developed and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics (DITE), Government of West Bengal.

On 19th July, 2026, STCL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of West Bengal for collaboration with the Yatri Sathi platform. Under the MoU, Bharat Taxi extends support in the areas of driver enrolment, cooperative membership, driver welfare and public outreach.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

(Release ID: 2298395)

headline: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
fullText:
Ministry of Cooperation

AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL

12 AUG 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Cooperation has set up Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing, distribution and strategic research & development of quality seeds with a clear vision to build a strong, farmer-centric seed system through a cooperative-led structure.

Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the 'Bharat Beej' brand for distribution across the country. Further, BBSSL has undertaken initiatives for developing production and quality-testing requirements for vegetable seeds in accordance with the prescribed seed quality and regulatory standards.

During the financial year 2025–26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through its associated seed-producing farmers under the seed production programme for the 'Bharat Beej' brand. The programme facilitates farmers' participation in organised seed production and provides technical support for the production of seeds in accordance with the prescribed quality and certification standards.

For the conservation of traditional indigenous varieties, BBSSL has initiated a programme in Uttarakhand focusing on the identification, conservation, multiplication and documentation of such varieties. BBSSL's activities include the expansion of domestic seed production, conservation of indigenous genetic resources, and distribution of quality seeds through the cooperative network, thereby contributing to the objective of reducing the country's dependence on imported seeds and strengthening self-reliance in the seed sector.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

(Release ID: 2298385)
